item.title: PYQ ACC 305
item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester / 6th Semester (Selected) Standard Instructions: Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially. Time: 4 Hours | Total Marks: 75Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) Define 'Assurance Engagement' and explain the key elements of an assurance engagement. [04] (b) Differentiate between reasonable and limited assurance. Can an audit of financial statements provide absolute assurance? Justify your answer with appropriate reasons. [04] (c) Describe the meaning of the "expectations gap" in the context of auditing. Suggest appropriate steps that may help in minimizing the expectations gap between auditors and users of financial statements. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) Contrast between audit and assurance. [05] (b) Compare and contrast between continuous and periodic audit. [05] (b) Who can be a statutory auditor? Name Big Four audit firms of the world. [05] (c) Mention the non-audit professional services offered by an auditor. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (b) Compare and contrast between continuous and periodic audit. [05] (c) What are the limitations of audit? Explain. [05] (b) What should be the traits of an Auditor? [05] (c) Mention the non-audit professional services offered by an auditor. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (b) What do limited and negative assurance mean? [03] (c) Discuss the most common types of assurance services. [06] (a) What is audit expectation gap? What are the causes behind the audit expectation gap? [05] (b) How can you explain the Agency relationships in Auditing? [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (a) Explain the main objectives of an audit with imperative purposes. [04] (c) Distinguish between internal audit and external audit. [03] (d) Establish relationships among auditing, attest and assurance services. [04] (a) Describe the three main phases of the audit. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (d) What is "Lowballing"? Point out the factors that an auditor should consider before accepting an audit engagement. [03] In professional audit practice, it is important to agree on the terms of engagement before any assignments are taken up. This ensures a clear understanding between the auditor and the client. Required: (a) Examine the key components of an audit engagement letter. [06] (b) Evaluate the factors to be considered during the assignment of the audit engagement team. [04] (c) Distinguish among appointment letter, proposal letter, and engagement letter. Discuss the conditions and stages at which they are prepared and state the objectives of each. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) What is audit risk? What are the different types of audit risk? [03] (c) Define the term ‘Assertion’ from the perspective of a financial audit. Describe the assertions related to ‘revenue’ and ‘receivables’ for conducting a financial audit. [07] (a) In accordance with ISA 500 - Audit Evidence, explain the meaning of ‘sufficiency’ and ‘appropriateness’ of audit evidence, and discuss the various audit procedures for obtaining such evidence. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) Enumerate in brief BSA-220 and BSA-500. [06] (c) What are the purposes of audit working papers? [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) Enumerate in brief BSA-200 and BSA-220. [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) What are the three components of the audit risk model? What is the relation between audit risk and detection risk? [05] (a) M/S Shimee Enterprise stocks thousands of items that range in value from Tk. 1,000 to Tk. 10,00,000. The inventory on hand represents a material portion of current assets. The merchandise items change according to the season and the promotional theme adopted by the stores' management for the year. Merchandise is ordered up to four months in advance from Chinese and Korean suppliers. These special orders require M/S Shimee Enterprise to give the suppliers substantial deposits upon placement of the orders. Required: ii. Discuss the assertions being made by management about the inventory. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (a) What is qualitative materiality and what is quantitative materiality? What are considered appropriate bases when setting materiality? [05] (b) Define persuasive, corroborative and minimal evidence. Give examples of each type of evidence for trade receivables and PPE. [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (b) Briefly explain the components of the internal control system as set out in ISA 315, ‘Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement’. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (b) What is an audit program? State its importance, advantages, and disadvantages. [06] (a) The existence and operation of a good system of internal control can reduce the auditor's workload to a considerable extent. State how the auditor can bring about this reduction. [05] (b) On being appointed the auditor of a company for the first time, you find that the cashier also handles the books of account and the cash receipts are not being banked intact, but parts of these are being utilized for cash payments. Required: What would be your reaction? What recommendations would you make to the company in this connection? [05] (c) You have been appointed as the internal auditor of a company, and you have come across certain weaknesses in the internal control system. Draft a specimen form of Management Letter indicating at least five areas of weakness relating to internal control. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) What do you mean by internal control system? What are its different components? [05] (b) What do you suggest to make a financial control system robust and defensible? [06] (c) When does an internal control system fail to circumvent fraud? [04] ABC is a food manufacturing company. They have 10 factory sites and 2500 workers. They have grown very rapidly in recent years under the direction of Mr. X, who is a very dynamic character. He tries to operate on the lowest possible costs and sees internal control as himself and his factory managers. The company has recently moved into the production of a mass-produced food item and expected that they will grab a large market share. They have an audit committee (not liked by Mr. X) but no internal audit department. Required: (a) What advantages might accrue to the company if they set up an internal audit department? [04] (b) How might the auditors approach the audit? [04] (c) What specific duties are imposed on the auditor regarding internal control and internal audit? [04] (d) Distinguish briefly internal control, internal check and internal audit. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (c) Explain the preliminary risk assessment procedure of a client. [06] (b) The Client Inc. sells microwaves through an e-commerce retail website. Customers have 30 days to pay. To purchase microwaves through the website, customers need to register and get approved before their purchases. In addition, customers who have a balance over the approved credit limit need the approval from the senior manager to continue the sales process. The auditor is satisfied that controls over the account registration process exist and the control design is adequate. However, the auditor finds that in some cases, customers who have a balance over the approved credit limit can continue to purchase microwaves successfully before they get approval from the senior manager. Required: i. What are the seven generally accepted objectives of internal control as related to the recording of transactions? [05] ii. Identify the weakness and complete the logic diagram for the above case. [05] (b) Explain how a statutory auditor of a company can apply analytical procedures at the planning phase of audit. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (c) What do you mean by fraud risk? From the following transactions identify whether it is 'financial reporting fraud' or 'misappropriation of assets fraud': i. Using company car for personal use ii. Delaying expenses, bringing forward revenues iii. Recording Fictitious revenues iv. Theft of stocks by employees v. Understating expenses [06] (b) Scenario: The following is the pre-audited financial information of ABC Company from 2017 to 2020. Required: Use analytical procedures and identify risky accounts. [10]Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) Describe how risks in IT systems, if not mitigated, could have an impact on audit. [05] (b) Briefly mention the reasons why IT should be considered relevant to an audit of financial statements. [05] (c) What are the different testing methods used when auditing in an automated environment? Which is the most effective and efficient method of testing? [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (b) Your firm XYZ & Co. Chartered Accountants, has been appointed as the auditor of Merry Company Limited (MCL) for the financial year ended 31 March 2025. You have been assigned as the engagement manager. During discussions with management, you were informed that MCL has recently received a significant number of requests for credit notes due to customers alleging that goods were received in poor condition. Therefore, Management of MCL intends to strengthen controls over the dispatch of goods and confirmation of their condition upon delivery. Again, you were informed that the directors of MCL have recently discovered that the store manager has been committing fraud. As part of her responsibilities, she was in charge of ordering inventory. She created fictitious purchase orders to non-existent suppliers, recorded false goods received notes for deliveries that never occurred, and submitted fake supplier invoices to the accounts department for payment. These invoices were subsequently paid by the company. MCL has also experienced a history of inventory theft. As a result, the directors have decided to strengthen the internal control system over the inventory ordering process to ensure that only goods genuinely required for business purposes are purchased. Required: i. Identify the audit risks associated with the dispatch and recording of delivered goods at MCL and suggest appropriate audit procedures to address the identified risks in relation to the dispatch and recording of goods. ii. Identify the audit risks associated with the ordering of inventories for MCL and suggest appropriate audit procedures to address the identified risks in relation to the ordering of inventories. [10] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) What do you understand by valuation of assets? [05] (b) How would you audit the following assets? i. Stock in trade ii. Intangible assets iii. Cash and cash equivalents [10] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) What is vouching? Discuss the features of vouching. State the important considerations before conducting vouching. [05] (b) While auditing the accounts of a trading concern, how would you examine that all liabilities incurred before the close of the year in respect of wages, freight and traveler's commission have been included in the accounts? [05] (c) What are the general considerations for evaluation and verification of assets? [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) M/S Shimee Enterprise stocks thousands of items that range in value from Tk. 1,000 to Tk. 10,00,000. The inventory on hand represents a material portion of current assets. The merchandise items change according to the season and the promotional theme adopted by the stores' management for the year. Merchandise is ordered up to four months in advance from Chinese and Korean suppliers. These special orders require M/S Shimee Enterprise to give the suppliers substantial deposits upon placement of the orders. Required: i. What are the inherent risks for M/S Shimee Enterprise inventory? [04] (b) Consider the following "what can go wrong" (WCGW) events. Explain what assertions and preventive control actions you need to take as an auditor against these WCGW: i. Sales occur that are not recoverable. ii. Fictitious employees are paid. iii. Sales are recorded at an incorrect value. iv. Transactions are classified and coded to incorrect accounts. [08] (a) What precautions should be taken by the auditor while applying test check techniques? [05] (c) While applying the Substantive Analytical Procedures what techniques can be used by the statutory auditor of a company to obtain sufficient and appropriate audit evidence? [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (a) Name two assertions that are significant for cash. Describe the substantive procedures that are always performed for cash. [05] (a) Ms. Rupa is the auditor in charge of XYZ Company. At the end of 2020, XYZ Company had Tk. 1,00,000 account receivables on its balance sheet. Rupa conducted confirmation with several major customers for Tk. 50,000 account receivables. Rupa was satisfied with the outcomes of confirmation and concluded that there was no material misstatement in account receivables. Required: i. Which assertion of account receivables may be violated? ii. How should Rupa verify the violated assertion? [05] (b) Mr. Dev is a junior staff of Chattolla CPA firm and is verifying sales invoices. There are 12 invoices and he wants to choose 4 invoices for test. His strategy is to first stratify the 12 invoices into 4 stratums based on the amount size. From each stratum, he will choose the invoice with median amount for test. Data: Required: i. Identify the invoice number in each stratum. ii. Identify the 4 invoices Mr. Dev would choose. [10] (a) Draw a sequence of testing purchases. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) Briefly discuss the duties of auditors according to Section 213 of the Companies Act, 1994. [05] (b) An auditor discovers a material misstatement in a client’s financial statements but is under pressure from the client to overlook it, as it could jeopardize a significant contract. Required: In this scenario, how should the auditor respond to this situation, considering the ethical standards for professional accountants? [05] (c) State the objectives, powers, and functions of the Financial Reporting Council under sections 7 and 8 of the Financial Reporting Act, 2015. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (c) What is FRC? What are its jurisdictions? [05] (a) Explain the role of Arthur Andersen in relation to the collapse of Enron. [05] (b) Elucidate the IFAC Guidelines of ethics for professional accountants. [05] (c) What is an audit committee? How can it ensure the integrity of internal and external audit work? [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) Discuss the main types of errors and frauds. [05] (a) Define ethics. What do you mean by professional ethics? [05] (b) Elucidate the IFAC Guidelines of ethics for professional accountants. [05] (c) What are the liabilities of an auditor as per Caparo Industries VS Dickman? [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) List down and explain the "five fundamental ethical principles" included in the code of Accounting Professional and Ethical Standards (APES) - 110. [05] (b) Discuss different kinds of threats to auditors' independence. [05] (c) You are the auditor in charge of ABC Company. During the audit, you found that one junior staff, Mr. Abhi, has invested a lot of money in ABC Company. Mr. Abhi also asked many of his friends and family members to buy shares of ABC Company. Currently, Mr. Abhi is in charge of the cash account. Required: Identify and explain the threat to auditor independence in the above case. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (b) Enumerate different categories of threats faced by auditors. [04] Mr. Abhi is the auditor of AAA company in 2019. During the audit period, AAA company just appointed a new Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mr. Sam. Abhi and Sam are close friends from college. They have known each other for 20 years. Selected Transactions / Events: (a) During the audit, Abhi found that many of the sales invoices were missing and some incomplete documentation. He intended to issue a disclaimer of audit opinion. However, Mr. Sam (CEO of AAA Company) asked Abhi to ignore these invoices and to issue an unqualified audit opinion. Otherwise, AAA Company will either pay lower audit fees or change him as an auditor next year. Abhi followed the advice of Sam. (b) It was Abhi's birthday. Sam offered free Bangladesh Vs Australia Grand Final T20 World Cup tickets for Abhi and his family as a birthday gift. Abhi accepted the gift from Sam. (c) Sam wanted to increase AAA company's sales but he was having some difficulties in finding new customers. He asked Abhi for his advice. Abhi had the names and contact details of some companies that might be interested in buying AAA company's products. Abhi's list of companies and their contact details was made up of customers of a previous client. Abhi gave the list to Sam. (d) During the audit, Abhi found that one junior staff, Krish, has invested a lot of money in AAA Company. Krish also asked many of his friends and family members to buy shares from AAA Company. Currently, Krish is in charge of confirming the cash account. Required: In each situation, identify the threats to the "Auditor's Independence" and explain why. [15] (b) Discuss in brief the principles of the code of conduct as framed by IFAC. [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) You are the auditor of Meghna Vehicle PLC, whose main activity is to buy and sell various types of motor vehicles. During the current year the company has suffered a significant fall in sales and abnormal increase of finance cost which has led to a net loss. The company is also experiencing cash flow problems. The draft financial statements show a loss for the current year but the forecast indicates a return to profitability in the upcoming financial year, as the directors are optimistic about the injection of a sufficient amount of fresh capital. Required: i. Describe the auditor’s responsibilities in relation to management’s assessment of the entity’s ability to continue as a going concern. ii. Identify the events or conditions that may cast significant doubt on an entity’s ability to continue as a going concern. [08] (b) There are certain general matters that are required to be included in a management representation letter. In accordance with ISA 580 – Written Representations, describe these general matters that management is expected to confirm in the representation letter. [03] (c) Briefly explain the contents of an auditor's report in accordance with ISA 700 – Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements. [04] (a) A modified audit opinion is issued when the auditor concludes, based on the audit evidence obtained, that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement. In cases of material misstatement, there are two types of modified audit opinions that may be expressed. Describe these two types of audit opinions. [05] (b) A modified audit opinion is issued when the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to conclude that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. In situations involving a limitation of scope, two types of modified audit opinions may be expressed. Describe these two types of audit opinions. [04] (c) Define the following terms as used in the Independent Auditor’s Report: Key Audit Matters (KAM) Emphasis of Matter paragraph Other Matter paragraph [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) State the basic features of an audit report. [05] (b) What is KAM, and state the requirements of determining and communicating KAM by the auditor as per ISA 701: Communicating Key Audit Matters in the independent auditor's report. [05] (c) State the circumstances and type of modifications to the auditor's opinion required as per ISA 705: Modifications to the opinion in the independent auditor's report. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 305 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) What is meant by auditor's report? [02] (b) Discuss the characteristics of a good audit report. [05] (c) How many types of audit report may be submitted by a company auditor and in what circumstances? Discuss briefly. [08] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) Mr. Shreyaan is the auditor of XYZ company. During the audit of the 2021 annual report, one branch office of XYZ company was destroyed by fire. Because of the fire, Mr. Shreyaan is unable to find some sales invoices (about 2% of total sales) and there is no backup in the company. Without the invoices, Mr. Shreyaan is also unable to contact the customers for confirmation purposes. He has access to the remaining 98% of invoices, and he believes there is no material misstatement in these invoices. Required: In the above case, which type of audit opinion Mr. Shreyaan would issue and why? [06] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 309 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (b) What is going concern assumptions? List down the factors that indicate the going concern assumptions may be at risk. [04] (c) Describe the situation under which an auditor needs to issue an adverse opinion or disclaimer of opinion. [04] (c) Explain the contents of a complete audit report as per BSA 700. [06]

item.title: PYQ ACC 304
item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester Standard Instructions: Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially. Time: 4 Hours | Total Marks: 75Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (d) Define manufacturing concern. What are the features of manufacturing concerns? [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) Define cost and cost accounting? [03] (c) Describe how standard costing and budgeting are used in cost control. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) Define financial accounting and cost accounting. Explain the relationship among financial accounting, cost accounting and management accounting. [05] (b) What are the methods of costing? Explain each of them in brief giving an example of an enterprise in which each may be suitable. [05] (c) How the following techniques of cost accounting are used in ascertain and controlling cost: i. Absorption costing [01] ii. Marginal costing [01] iii. Life cycle costing [01] iv. Target costing [01] v. Standard costing [01] vi. Budgeting [01] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 (a) Define cost accounting. Explain the relationship between cost accounting and financial accounting. [05] (b) The limitations of financial accounting lead to the origin and development of cost accounting - Explain. [05] (c) What are the different methods of costing? Explain each of them in brief with examples of enterprises to which it is applicable. [05] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (b) Data: The following particulars have been extracted from the accounting records of Peterson Manufacturing Ltd. for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024: Additional Information for the Year: Purchases of direct materials: Tk. 74,000 Direct manufacturing labor: Tk. 22,000 Direct expenses (Specialized tool hire): Tk. 5,000 Indirect manufacturing labor: Tk. 17,000 Plant insurance: Tk. 7,000 Depreciation—plant, building, and equipment: Tk. 11,000 Repairs and maintenance—plant: Tk. 3,000 Marketing, distribution, and customer-service costs: Tk. 91,000 General and administrative costs: Tk. 24,000 Sales of scrap (from production): Tk. 2,000 Profit: 25% on Sales Required: Compute the following: Cost of materials used Prime cost Manufacturing Overhead Costs Cost of goods manufactured Cost of goods sold Cost of sales Total Sales value [10] (a) Data: TSN Office Equipment manufactures and sells metal shelving. It began operations on January 1, 2020. Costs incurred for 2020 are as follows (V stands for variable; F stands for fixed): Direct materials used: Tk. 140,000 V Direct manufacturing labor costs: 22,000 V Plant energy costs: 5,000 V Indirect manufacturing labor costs: 18,000 V Indirect manufacturing labor costs: 14,000 F Other indirect manufacturing costs: 8,000 V Other indirect manufacturing costs: 26,000 F Marketing, distribution, and customer service costs: 120,000 V Marketing, distribution, and customer service costs: 43,000 F Administrative costs: 54,000 F Variable manufacturing costs are variable with respect to units produced. Variable marketing, distribution, and customer-service costs are variable with respect to units sold.Inventory data are as follows: Materials Control, beginning: 0 lb Materials Control, ending: 2,300 lbs (pound) Work-in-Process, beginning: 0 units Work-in-Process, ending: 0 units Finished Goods, beginning: 0 units Finished Goods, ending: ? units Additional Information: Production in 2020 was 100,000 units. Two pounds of direct materials are used to make one unit of finished product. Revenues in 2020 were Tk. 473,200. The selling price per unit and the purchase price per pound of direct materials were stable throughout the year. The company's ending inventory of finished goods is carried at the average unit manufacturing cost for 2020. Finished-goods inventory at December 31, 2020, was Tk. 20,970. Required: - i. Calculate direct materials inventory, total cost, December 31, 2020. [1.5] - ii. Calculate finished-goods inventory, total units, December 31, 2020. [2.5] - iii. Calculate selling price in 2020. [1.5] - iv. Calculate operating income for 2020. [2.5] (b) Surge Automotive Ltd. specializes in producing a high-capacity off-road vehicle called the "Terrain." The company has provided the following manufacturing cost data for the upcoming budget year: Fixed Costs (Annual): Plant administration and management salaries: $2,160,000 per year Cost of leasing production facility: $1,440,000 per year Variable Costs (Per Unit): Direct manufacturing labor wages: $1,500 per unit Direct materials: Engine and chassis ($3,500); Specialty tires ($200 per tire). Each vehicle requires 6 tires (including two spares). Step-Variable Cost (Monthly): Monthly Environmental Compliance Fee (based on the total number of tires used in production): 0–500 tires: $30,000 501–1,000 tires: $75,000 More than 1,000 tires: $180,000 Required: i. Compute the total manufacturing cost and the average manufacturing cost per unit if the company produces 80 vehicles in a month. [03] ii. Compute the total manufacturing cost and the average manufacturing cost per unit if the company increases production to 180 vehicles in a month. [03] iii. Briefly explain the primary reasons why the average manufacturing cost per unit differs between these two production levels. [01] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) Define Cost Objects, Cost Drivers, Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, and Period Costs. [05] (b) Data: The following particulars have been extracted from the books of Alfa Ltd. Required: You are asked to compute: i. Cost of materials used ii. Prime cost iii. Works cost iv. Cost of goods manufactured v. Cost of goods sold vi. Cost of sales vii. Sales [10] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (b) Explain the difference between cost and expense. [03] Data: The following cost and inventory data are taken from the accounting records of Mason Company for the year just ended:Required: (a) Prepare a schedule of cost of goods manufactured. [05] (b) Prepare an Income Statement. [03] (c) Assume the company produced equivalent of 10,000 units of product during the year just completed. What was the average cost per unit for direct materials? What was the average cost per unit for fixed manufacturing overhead? [03] (d) Assume that the company expects to produce 15,000 units of product during the coming year. What average cost per unit and what total cost would you expect the company to incur for direct materials at this level of activity? For fixed manufacturing overhead? Assume that the direct material is a variable cost. [04] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2022Data: The following cost and inventory data are taken from the accounting records of Mason Company for the year ended 31st December 2021:Required: (a) Prepare a schedule of cost of goods manufactured. (b) Prepare an Income Statement. (c) Assume the company produced equivalent of 10,000 units of product during the year just completed. What was the average cost per unit for direct materials? What was the average cost per unit for fixed manufacturing overhead? (d) Assume that the company expects to produce 15,000 units of product during the coming year. What average cost per unit and what total cost would you expect the company to incur for direct materials at this level of activity? For fixed manufacturing overhead? Assume that the direct material is a variable cost. [15] Write short notes on the following: (b) Cost centre and cost unit. [03] (c) Sunk cost and opportunity cost. [03] (e) Comprehensive income statement. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2021Data: The following information has been taken from the records of Niba Company:Requirements: (a) Prepare a statement of goods manufactured. (b) Prepare a statement of goods sold. (c) Prepare a statement of comprehensive income. [15] Write short notes on: (d) Product cost and period cost. [03] (e) Cost and expense. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) M/s Global Tech Ltd. manufactures high-precision industrial valves. The company provides the following information regarding one of its primary raw materials: Data: Annual Requirement: 10,000 units Cost of placing an order: Rs. 100 Purchase price per unit: Rs. 40 Inventory carrying cost: 20% per annum Lead Time for supply: 5 to 15 days Rate of Consumption: 15 units (Average) and 20 units (Maximum) per day. Required: i. Compute the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ). [04] ii. A supplier has offered a 2% discount on the purchase price if the company accepts a lot size of 2,500 units per order. Evaluate whether the company should accept this discount offer by preparing a comparative cost statement. [04] iii. Calculate the Re-order Level for this material. [02] (a) Data: Pran Company made the following materials purchases and issues during January. Inventory: January 1. 500 units @ Tk. 12.00 Receipts: January 6: 200 units @ Tk. 12.50 January 10: 400 units @ Tk. 13.00 January 25: 500 units @ Tk. 14.00 Issues: January 15: 560 units January 27: 400 units. Required: Compute the cost of materials consumed and the cost assigned to the inventory at the end of the month, using the perpetual inventory system and: i. Average costing. [2.5] ii. FIFO costing. [2.5] (b) Data: LeMaster Company would like to determine the safety stock to maintain a product, so that the lowest combination of stockout cost and carrying cost would result. Each stockout will cost Tk. 75; the carrying cost for each safety stock unit will be Tk. 1; the product will be ordered five times a year. The following probabilities of running out of stock during an order period are associated with various safety stock levels: Required: Determine the combined stockout and safety stock carrying cost associated with each level and the recommended level of safety stock. [04] (c) Data: Evan Company has developed the following costs and other data pertaining to one of its raw materials: Normal use per day: 400 units Maximum use per day: 600 units Minimum use per day: 100 units Working day per year: 250 Lead time: 8 days Cost of placing an order: Tk. 20.00 Cost per unit of material: Tk. 2.50 Carrying cost percentage: 10% Required: Compute the following: i. Economic order quantity. [01] ii. Safety stock. [01] iii. Reorder point. [01] iv. Normal maximum inventory. [01] v. Absolute maximum inventory. [01] vi. Average normal inventory. [01] (a) Data: Dempsey Inc. is a retailer operating in British Columbia. Dempsey uses the periodic inventory system. All sales returns from customers result in the goods being returned to inventory; the inventory is not damaged. Assume that there are no credit transactions; all amounts are settled in cash. You are provided with the following information for Dempsey Inc. for the month of January 2022: Required: i. For both i) FIFO (First-in, First-out) ii) Moving-average cost (Round the weighted-average unit cost to three decimal places) cost flow assumptions, calculate (a) cost of goods sold, (b) ending inventory, and (c) gross profit. [06] ii. Compare the results for the three cost flow assumptions. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) Data: ABC & Sons, Inc. wants to determine the appropriate safety stock level for a product to minimize the total cost from stockouts and carrying inventory. The cost of a stockout is $30 per occurrence, and the annual carrying cost for each unit of safety stock is $0.50. The product is ordered 10 times per year. The probabilities of running out of stock during an order cycle based on different safety stock levels are as follows: Required: Calculate the total cost (stockout cost plus carrying cost) for each safety stock level and recommend the optimal safety stock level. [04] (b) The Knot manufactures men's neckwear at its Spartanburg plant. The Knot is considering implementing a JIT production system. The following are the estimated costs and benefits of JIT production: Data: Annual additional tooling costs $250,000 annually. Average inventory would decline by 80% from the current level of $1,000,000. Insurance, space, materials-handling, and setup costs, which currently total $400,000 annually, would decline by 20%. The emphasis on quality inherent in JIT production would reduce rework costs by 25%. The Knot currently incurs $160,000 in annual rework costs. Improved product quality under JIT production would enable The Knot to raise the price of its product by $2 per unit. The Knot sells 100,000 units each year. The Knot's required rate of return on inventory investment is 15% per year. Required: Calculate the net benefit or cost to The Knot if it adopts JIT production at the Spartanburg plant. Also, state some non-financial and qualitative factors that should be considered when adopting JIT production. [05] (c) Data: The following information is to be used in costing inventory on May 31: Required: Compute the cost of materials used and the cost assigned to the May 31st inventory by each of these perpetual inventory costing methods: i. FIFO ii. Weighted average method [06] (a) Data: M/s Tubes Ltd. are the manufacturers of picture tubes for T.V. The following are the details of their operation during the year 2024: Cost of placing a purchase order is $20 Number of units to be purchased during the year is 5,000 Purchase price per unit inclusive of transportation cost is $50 Annual cost of storage per unit is $5 Details of lead time: Average: 10 days, Maximum: 15 days, Minimum: 5 days. For emergency purchases: 4 days. Rate of consumption: Average: 15 units per day, Maximum: 20 units per day. Required: Compute from the above: i. Re-ordering level ii. Maximum level iii. Minimum level iv. Danger level v. Re-order quantity [06] (b) Data: From the following particulars with respect to a particular item of materials of a manufacturing company, calculate the best quantity to order: The annual demand for the material is 4,000 tonnes. Stock holding costs are 20% of material cost p.a. The ordering cost is $6.00 per order. [06] (c) Define EOQ. State the key assumptions of the EOQ model. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) What do you understand by Economic order quantity? Explain with graph. [02] (b) What are the differences between bin card and stores ledger? [02] (c) Data: Maxim Limited manufactures a special product "Zed". The following particulars were collected for the current year: Monthly demand of Zed: 1,000 units. Cost of placing an order: $100. Annual carrying cost per unit: $15. Normal usage: 100 units per week. Maximum usage: 125 units per week. Minimum usage: 65 units per week. Reorder period: 4 to 6 weeks. Compute: i. Reorder quantity ii. Reorder level iii. Maximum level iv. Minimum level v. Average stock level [05] (d) Data: Exe Limited has received an offer of quantity discounts on its order of materials as under: The annual requirements for the materials are 10,000 tons. The ordering cost per order is $2,000 and stock holding cost estimated at 25 per cent of material cost per annum. You are required to compute the most economical purchase level. [06]Data: The following is the summary of the receipts and issues of material in a factory during December 2007: Dec 1: Opening balance 500 units @ Rs.25 per unit Dec 3: Issue 70 units Dec 4: Issue 100 units Dec 8: Issue 80 units Dec 13: Received from supplier 200 units @ Rs.24.50 per unit Dec 14: Returned to store 15 units @ Rs.24 per unit Dec 16: Issue 180 units Dec 20: Received from supplier 240 units @ Rs.24.75 per unit Dec 24: Issue 304 units Dec 25: Received from supplier 320 units @ Rs.24.50 per unit Dec 26: Issue 112 units Dec 27: Returned to store 12 units @ Rs.24.50 per unit Dec 28: Received from supplier 100 units @ Rs.25 per unit Shortages revealed: December 15th: shortage of 5 units December 27th: shortage of 8 units. Required: Prepare Store Ledger according to First in First Out Method (FIFO) for December 2007. [15]Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2022 (a) What do you understand by Economic Order Quantity? What are the factors to be considered in determining this quantity? Explain in brief. [03] (b) Data: Myler Tubes Limited are the manufacturer of picture tubes of Television. The following are the details of the operations during the current year: Average monthly market demands: 2,000 tubes Ordering cost: $100 per order Inventory carrying cost: 25% per annum Cost of tube: $400 per tube Normal usage: 100 tubes per week Minimum usage: 50 tubes per week Maximum usage: 200 tubes per week Lead time to supply: 6 to 8 weeks Compute from the above: i. Economic order quantity. If the supplier is willing to supply quarterly 1,300 units at a discount of 5 per cent, is it worth accepting? ii. Maximum stock level. iii. Minimum stock level and iv. Reorder level. [06] (c) Data: The purchase department of an organization has received an offer of quantity discounts on its order of materials as under: The annual requirement of the materials is 5000 tons. The delivery cost per order is $1,200 and the annual stock holding cost is estimated at 20 per cent of the average inventory.Required: Evaluate the following purchase options and advise which among them will be the most economical order quantity, presenting the information in a tabular form. The purchase quantity options to be considered are: 400 tons, 500 tons, 1,000 tons, 2000 tons, and 3,000 tons. [06] Write short notes on the following: (a) Bin card and Stores Ledger. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 310 | BBA 6th Semester 2021 Write short notes on: (b) IAS—2. [03] Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC 304 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) An employee working under a bonus scheme saves 4 hours in a job for which the standard time is 32 hours. Calculate the rate per hour worked and wages payable for the time taken under the following alternative schemes. (Award rate Tk. 1/- per hour) i. Employee receives an increase in the hourly rate based on the percentage of time saved to the time set. ii. A bonus of 10 per cent on award rate is payable when standard time (namely, 100 per cent efficiency) is achieved plus a further bonus of 1 per cent on award rate for each 1 per cent in excess of that 100 per cent efficiency. [05] (b) Data: Calculate the normal and overtime wages payable to a workman from the following data: Normal working hours per day is 8 hours. Normal rate per hour is Tk.10. item.title: ACC 303 Notes Module 1
item.description: Key Definition Statistical analysis is fundamental to modern business decision-making and econometric modeling. The term statistics carries two distinct definitions based on context: Plural Sense ("statistics"): Numerical facts, figures, or data collected for analysis (e.g., inflation rate of , quarterly GDP growth of , or average hourly wage of ). Singular Sense ("statistics"): The scientific discipline and methodology concerning the collection, organization, presentation, analysis, and interpretation of data to assist in making effective decisions under conditions of uncertainty. Statistical methods are formally bifurcated into two primary branches based on research objectives and data availability: Descriptive Statistics: Statistical procedures and graphical techniques utilized to organize, summarize, and present raw numerical data in an informative, structured format. Primary Tools: Frequency tables, histograms, bar charts, pie charts, scatter plots, measures of location (mean, median, mode), and measures of dispersion (variance, standard deviation, interquartile range). Scope: Confined strictly to the observed dataset; no probabilistic conclusions are extended to unobserved entities. Inferential Statistics: The body of statistical methods used to draw inferences, conclusions, or estimates about unknown population parameters based strictly on sample statistics. Primary Tools: Probability distributions, point and interval estimation, parametric and non-parametric hypothesis testing, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), and regression analysis. Scope: Evaluates risks and uncertainty by applying probability theory to quantify the margin of error (sampling error) inherent in generalizing from a sample to an entire population. To conduct empirical research, the domain of inquiry must be clearly conceptualized: Methodological Trade-offs: A Census eliminates sampling error because every population unit is examined. However, for large or infinite populations, a census is economically prohibitive, time-consuming, physically impossible (e.g., measuring lifespan of industrial batteries), or destructive (e.g., blood testing). Furthermore, censuses accumulate non-sampling and administrative errors as grows. A Sample Survey dramatically reduces data collection costs, accelerates research timelines, and allows deeper data probing. However, it introduces sampling error due to random variations between sample statistics and true population parameters. A variable is a quantity or characteristic that can take on different numerical values or categories across observations. Qualitative (Attribute/Categorical) Variable: A non-numeric characteristic where individual observations are classified into distinct categories (e.g., gender, PC brand preference, marital status, state of residence). Summarized using counts, frequencies, and percentages. Quantitative Variable: A variable that is expressed numerically. Discrete Quantitative Variable: A variable that can assume only distinct, clearly separated integer values with "gaps" between possible values. Discrete variables typically arise from counting operations (e.g., number of bedrooms in a house: ; number of defective components per batch). Continuous Quantitative Variable: A variable that can assume any real numerical value within a given continuous interval. Continuous variables result from measuring operations and depend on the precision of the measuring instrument (e.g., flight duration, atmospheric pressure, student GPA, body weight). The mathematical level of measurement determines the appropriate statistical tools, charts, and mathematical operations that can validly be applied to a variable.Research in business and economics is a systematic, multi-step process designed to solve problems and establish empirical relationships. Defining the Target Universe/Population: Specifying whether the universe is finite ( is known and countable) or infinite ( is theoretically unlimited). Identifying the Sampling Unit: Selecting the elementary unit to be sampled (e.g., geographic region, household, firm, or individual). Establishing the Sampling Frame (Source List): Constructing or obtaining a comprehensive, accurate list of all sampling units in the population. Determining Sample Size (): Calculating an optimal sample size that balances statistical precision, confidence level, population variability, and cost. Selecting the Sampling Procedure: Deciding between probability and non-probability sampling designs. Under non-probability sampling, elements do not have a known or equal probability of selection. Selection depends on human judgment or convenience: Purposive / Judgment Sampling: Items are selected deliberately by the researcher based on personal expertise and belief that the sample represents the population. Limitation Highly vulnerable to researcher bias; sampling error cannot be calculated. Convenience Sampling: Selecting population units that are easily accessible (e.g., surveying students in a single cafeteria). Limitation Generates severely biased results that cannot be generalized to broader populations. Quota Sampling: Interviewers are given specific quotas to fill across non-overlapping categories (e.g., 50 males, 50 females) but selection within quotas is left to interviewer discretion. Every element in the population has a known, non-zero probability of being included in the sample, ensuring unbiased estimation and allowing formal mathematical calculation of sampling error. Simple Random Sampling (SRS): Each possible sample combination of size from a finite population has an equal probability of selection: Implemented using lottery draws or computerized random number generators (e.g., Tippett's random number tables). Systematic Random Sampling: Elements are selected at equal numeric intervals through an ordered sampling frame. Procedure: Calculate sampling interval . Select a random starting integer between and . The sample consists of elements: Critical Risk If the sampling frame possesses a hidden periodic structure or cycle that matches , the sample will suffer from severe systematic bias. Stratified Random Sampling: Used when a population is non-homogeneous. The population is divided into non-overlapping, internally homogeneous subgroups called strata (). Independent simple random samples are drawn from each stratum. Proportional Allocation: Stratum sample size is directly proportional to stratum population size : Optimum (Neyman) Allocation: Accounts for differences in both stratum size () and stratum variability (). Stratum sample size is computed as: (Allocates larger sample sizes to larger and more variable strata, minimizing the variance of the sample estimator for a fixed total sample size). Cluster Sampling: The population is divided into naturally occurring, internally heterogeneous subgroups called clusters (e.g., geographic blocks, corporate branches). A random sample of clusters is chosen, and either all elements within chosen clusters are examined (one-stage) or simple random samples are drawn within chosen clusters (two-stage). Trade-off: Highly cost-effective for geographically dispersed populations, but yields higher sampling error than SRS for a given sample size due to intra-cluster correlation. Area Sampling: A primary form of cluster sampling where clusters are defined by geographical subdivisions (e.g., counties, census tracts). Multi-Stage Sampling: Sequential random sampling across hierarchical levels in large-scale national surveys (e.g., Primary Stage: States Secondary Stage: Districts Tertiary Stage: Towns Final Stage: Households). Sequential Sampling: Sample size is not fixed prior to the survey; items are drawn sequentially until cumulative evidence satisfies a statistical decision rule under statistical quality control. Sampling Error: The random variation or difference between a sample statistic () and the true population parameter (): Sampling errors occur purely due to chance. The expected value of sampling error is zero. As sample size increases, sampling error decreases at the rate of . Non-Sampling (Systematic) Error: Errors caused by human mistake, flawed sampling frame, ambiguous survey questions, non-response bias, uncalibrated instruments, or incorrect data recording. Non-sampling errors do not decrease with larger sample sizes and can severely distort research conclusions. The sampling distribution of the sample mean is a probability distribution consisting of all possible sample means () calculated from all possible random samples of a specified size drawn from a given population . Expected Value (Unbiasedness): The mean of the sampling distribution of sample means () is strictly equal to the true population mean (): Standard Error of the Mean (): The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of sample means, measuring the dispersion of sample estimates around the population mean: When sampling is conducted without replacement from a finite population of size , and the sample size constitutes more than of the population (), the standard error formula must be multiplied by the Finite Population Correction (FPC) factor:Finite Population Correction (FPC) Impact of FPC: As the sample size approaches population size , , reflecting the fact that as , uncertainty vanishes and the sampling error approaches zero.Fundamental Theorem: The Central Limit Theorem The Central Limit Theorem is the foundational theorem of inferential statistics and classical econometrics. Statement: If random samples of size are selected from any population possessing a finite mean and a finite variance , as the sample size increases (), the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches a normal distribution with mean and variance , regardless of the structural shape of the underlying population probability distribution. Using the CLT, any sample mean from a large sample () can be standardized into a standard normal random variable : Sample Space (): The set of all possible outcomes of a chance experiment. Event (): A specific subset of outcomes in . Axioms of Probability: for every event . . For mutually exclusive events : . A random variable taking distinct values with discrete PDF : A random variable defined over a continuous interval with PDF : Exception / Rule Fundamental Property: For any continuous random variable, the probability of assuming an exact single value is zero: . When two random variables and are observed simultaneously: Joint PDF : Discrete: Continuous: Marginal Probability Density Functions: Marginal PDF of : (discrete) or (continuous). Marginal PDF of : (discrete) or (continuous). Conditional Probability Density Functions: Statistical Independence: Random variables and are statistically independent if and only if their joint density equals the product of their marginal densities for all : Discrete: Continuous: for any constant . . (always holds, regardless of independence). If and are statistically independent: . Properties: If and are independent: . If and are independent, (note: converse is not generally true unless are bivariate normal). -th Central Moment: Skewness (): Measures lack of symmetry (3rd standardized moment): : Symmetric distribution. : Positively skewed (long right tail). : Negatively skewed (long left tail). Kurtosis (): Measures peakness and tail-heaviness (4th standardized moment): : Mesokurtic (Standard Normal Distribution). : Leptokurtic (Pied/slim peak, fat/heavy tails). : Platykurtic (Flat peak, thin tails). Numerical Problem 1: Stratified Sampling & Neyman Optimum Allocation Context: A business research institute needs to draw a sample of firms from a total population of companies categorized into three financial strata: Stratum 1 (Large-cap): , Stratum 2 (Mid-cap): , Stratum 3 (Small-cap): , Required: Compute the stratum sample sizes () under Proportional Allocation. Compute the stratum sample sizes () under Optimum (Neyman) Allocation. Provide the theoretical justification for why Neyman allocation differs from Proportional allocation. Part 1: Proportional Allocation Under proportional allocation, the proportion of elements sampled from each stratum equals the proportion of the population in that stratum: Stratum 1: Stratum 2: Stratum 3: Check: . Part 2: Optimum (Neyman) Allocation Under Neyman allocation, the sample size allocated to stratum is proportional to the product of stratum population size () and stratum standard deviation (): Step 1: Compute for each stratum: Stratum 1: Stratum 2: Stratum 3: Sum: Step 2: Compute for each stratum: Stratum 1: Stratum 2: Stratum 3: Check: . Part 3: Theoretical Justification Proportional allocation assigns sample size purely based on stratum size, ignoring internal variation. Neyman optimum allocation assigns a significantly larger sample size to Stratum 1 ( vs ) because Stratum 1 exhibits much higher internal variability ( vs ). By taking larger samples from more variable strata, Neyman allocation minimizes the overall variance of the stratified sample mean estimator for a fixed total sample size . Numerical Problem 2: Central Limit Theorem & Sampling Error Probability Analysis Context: An airline tracks the annual maintenance cost of commercial passenger jets. The population mean annual maintenance cost is with a population standard deviation of . The underlying distribution of maintenance costs across individual aircraft is strongly positively skewed. A simple random sample of aircraft is selected. Required: Describe the shape of the sampling distribution of the sample mean and state the governing statistical theorem. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean (). Compute the probability that the sample mean maintenance cost falls between and . Compute the probability that the sampling error exceeds in absolute magnitude. By the Central Limit Theorem (CLT), the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal: Part 2: Standard Error Calculation The standard error of the mean is . item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester Standard Format: 4 Hours | 75 Marks | Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially.Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) "Investment, financing and dividend decisions are all interrelated." Comment. [03] (b) "To avoid the problem of shortage and surplus of funds, what is required in Financial management? Name the concept and explain four points of importance. [04] (c) Explain why the following statements appearing in the objectives of two well-known listed companies are not necessarily contradictory? [04] "We never confuse why we exist - to create the maximum possible returns to our shareholders." "In everything the company does, it is committed to creating wealth always with integrity, for our employees, customers, suppliers and the community in which we operate." (d) Why do managers and other agents of the shareholders, such as employees sometimes have different objectives? [04] (a) Explain the following statement: "Most investors are risk averse." [03] (b) "An asset held as part of a portfolio is generally less risky than the same asset held in isolation." Do you agree with this statement? Why or why not? [03] (c) BSCCL stock has an expected return of 10 percent, a beta coefficient of 0.9, and a standard deviation of expected returns of 35 percent. BSC stock has an expected return of 12.5 percent, a beta coefficient of 1.2, and a standard deviation of expected returns of 25 percent. The risk-free rate is 6 percent, and the market risk premium is 5 percent. i. Calculate each stock's coefficient of variation. ii. Which stock is riskier for diversified investors? iii. Calculate each stock's required rate of return. iv. On the basis of the two stocks' expected and required returns, which stock would be most attractive to a diversified investor? v. Calculate the required return of a portfolio that has tk. 7,500 invested in BSCCL stock and tk. 2,500 invested in BSC stock. vi. If the market risk premium increased to 6 percent, which of the two stocks would have the largest increase in their required return? [09] (a) Assume that there are three stocks in a portfolio- stock-1, stock-2, and stock-3. The expected return vector of this portfolio is and the weighting vector of this portfolio is where, The variances of stock-1, stock-2, and stock-3 are 12%, 7%, and 9% respectively and the correlation coefficients between stock-1 and stock-2, stock-1 and stock-3, and stock-2 and stock-3 are 0.2, -0.6, and -0.3. Required: i. Compute portfolio return (use vector multiplication). [02] ii. Compute portfolio risk (use vector multiplication). [07] iii. Compute minimum and maximum portfolio return. [02] (b) A firm's equity beta is 0.9. The risk-free rate is 4% and the expected market return is 11%. Calculate the cost of equity. [02] (c) A firm's stock is currently being traded at $40. The expected dividend next year is $2.50 and dividends are expected to grow at 5% per year indefinitely. Estimate the cost of equity capital. [02] (a) A two-year bond has a face value of $1,000 and a coupon rate of 8% paid annually. The probability of default each year is 4%. If default occurs, the recovery value is $500. The bond is issued at par. Estimate the expected cost of debt. [05] (b) A project is fully financed by equity and has the same business risk as three pure-play comparable firms that are also all-equity financed. The equity betas of the comparable firms are 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6, respectively. The risk-free rate is 4% and the market risk premium is 8%. Estimate the appropriate discount rate for the project. [05] (c) How can investors be classified in terms of their risk preference? [05] (a) A firm operates in a perfect capital market where the Modigliani-Miller (MM) assumptions hold and there are no taxes. The firm's overall cost of capital (cost of assets) is 12 percent. The firm is financed with $4 million of debt and $6 million of equity. The cost of debt is 7 percent. Find the cost of equity. [02] (b) An investor owns 1% of an unlevered firm worth $5,000,000. The firm decides to remain unlevered, but the investor wants leverage equivalent to a firm with 40% debt. How can the investor create homemade leverage? [03] (c) A firm is financed with both debt and equity. The market value of debt is $5 million and the market value of equity is also $5 million. The required rate of return on equity is 14 percent, while the cost of debt is 8 percent. The corporate tax rate is 30 percent. In addition, investors face personal taxes: interest income is taxed at 40 percent, whereas equity income is taxed at 20 percent. Find the firm's weighted average cost of capital (WACC) considering both corporate and personal taxes. [05] (d) A firm generates an annual EBIT of $1,200,000. The required return on assets for an unlevered firm is 10 percent. The corporate tax rate is 30 percent. The firm plans to issue permanent debt of $4,000,000. In addition to corporate taxes, investors face personal taxes: Personal tax rate on interest income = 35% Personal tax rate on equity income = 15% Required: i. Find the value of the unlevered firm. [02] ii. Find the value of the levered firm considering both corporate and personal taxes. [03] (a) A company has reported earnings per share of $4.00 and maintains a dividend payout ratio of 40 percent. The company's return on equity is 15 percent, and the required rate of return on the stock is 12 percent. The company is expected to experience high growth for the next four years, after which it will settle into a stable growth rate of 5 percent indefinitely. Estimate the intrinsic value of the stock using the two-stage dividend discount model, where the high-growth rate is derived from the firm's sustainable growth rate. [04] (b) A company issues a $1,000 par bond, paying a 10% annual coupon semiannually for 6 years. The required annual rate of return is 12%. Determine the bond value. [03] (c) An investor purchases one European call option on a stock that is currently trading at $40 per share. The option has a strike price of $35 and a premium of $5, and it expires in three months. Determine the payoff and profit or loss at expiration for various possible stock prices: $30, $35, $40, $45, and $50 and plot the results in the graph. [05] (d) A stock is currently trading at $50. A European call option with a strike price of $55 expiring in 6 months is trading at $4.50, and a European put option with the same strike price and expiration is trading at $9.00. The risk-free interest rate for 6 months is 2% (continuously compounded). Verify whether put-call parity holds and explain the relationship between the call and put prices. [03] A firm is evaluating a proposal to install a new production machine to expand its operations. The project requires careful estimation of cash flows considering depreciation tax shield and interest tax shield.Project Information: Cost of new machine: USD 10,000,000 Installation and transportation cost: USD 1,000,000 Total initial investment: USD 11,000,000 The machine will be depreciated using the straight-line method over 5 years to a salvage value of USD 1,000,000. The project life is 5 years. Operating Information: Expected annual sales revenue: USD 6,000,000 Annual operating costs (excluding depreciation and interest): USD 3,000,000 Corporate tax rate: 30% The project will be financed as follows: 40% debt and 60% equity Loan amount will carry an interest rate of 10% per year The loan will be repaid in equal principal installments over 5 years Additional Information: Expected salvage value at the end of Year 5: USD 1,200,000 Working capital requirement: USD 500,000 (required at the beginning and fully recovered at the end of Year 5) Required rate of return (WACC): 12% Required: i. Estimate the initial cash flows of the project. [1] ii. Estimate the operating cash flows of the project. [5] iii. Estimate the terminal cash flows of the project. [3] iv. Based on the NPV, should the company accept the project? Justify your answer. [6] Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) What are the possible alternative financial goals of the organization? Which one do you recommend and why? [06] (b) Point out the decisions that are made by financial manager. Explain. [05] (c) What do mean by agency costs? How can this costs be minimized? [04] (a) Explain why you agree or disagree with this statement "Most investors are risk-averse". [03] (b) Consider the following information for Stocks A, B, and C. The returns on the three stocks are positively correlated, but they are not perfectly correlated. (That is, each of the correlation coefficients is between 0 and 1.) Fund Dhaka Ltd has one-third of its funds invested in each of the three stocks. The risk-free rate is 5.5%, and the market is in equilibrium. (That is, required returns equal expected returns.) Requirements: - i. What is the market risk premium ()? - ii. What is the beta of Fund Dhaka Ltd? - iii. What is the required return of Fund Dhaka Ltd? - iv. Would you expect the standard deviation of Fund Dhaka Ltd to be less than 15%, equal to 15%, or greater than 15%? Explain. [08] (c) A mutual fund manager has a Tk. 20 million portfolio with a beta of 1.7. The risk-free rate is 4.5%, and the market risk premium is 7%. The manager expects to receive an additional Tk. 5 million, which she plans to invest in a number of stocks. After investing the additional funds, she wants the fund's required return to be 15%. What should be the average beta of the new stocks added to the portfolio? [04] (a) General Electric Company (GEC) uses only debt and common equity. It can borrow unlimited amounts at an interest rate of as long as it finances at its target capital structure, which calls for 35% debt and 65% common equity. Its last dividend () was Tk 2.20, its expected constant growth rate is 6%, and its common stock sells for Tk 26. GEC's tax rate is 40%. Two projects are available: Project A has a rate of return of 12% and Project B's return is 11%. These two projects are equally risky and about as risky as the firm's existing assets. i. What is its cost of common equity? ii. What is the WACC? iii. Which projects should GEC accept? [08] (b) The KR Company's EPS was TK 6.50 in 2024, up from TK 4.42 in 2019. The company pays out 40% of its earnings as dividends, and its common stock sells for TK 36.00. i. Calculate the past growth rate in earnings. (Hint: This is a 5-year growth period.) ii. The last dividend was . Calculate the next expected dividend, , assuming that the past growth rate continues. iii. What is KR's cost of retained earnings, ? [07] (a) Explain this statement "Using financial leverage has both good and bad effects". [03] (b) Explain what asymmetric information means, and how signals affect capital structure decisions. [04] (c) A company currently has assets of Tk 5 million. The firm is 100 percent equity financed. The company currently has net income of Tk 1.5 million, and it pays out 40 percent of its net income as dividends. Both net income and dividends are expected to grow at a constant rate of 6 percent per year. There are 200,000 shares of stock outstanding, and it is estimated that the current cost of capital is 13.40 percent. The company is considering a recapitalization where it will issue Tk 1.5 million in debt and use the proceeds to repurchase stock. Investment bankers have estimated that if the company goes through with the recapitalization, its before-tax cost of debt will be 11 percent, and the cost of equity will rise to 14.5 percent. The company has a 40 percent federal tax rate. i. What is the current share price of the stock (before the recapitalization)? ii. Assuming that the company maintains the same payout ratio, what will be its stock price following the recapitalization? [08] (a) Delineate the alternative current asset financing policies with suitable diagram. [05] (b) What is cash conversion cycle? Define its three components. [03] (c) Christie Corporation is trying to determine the effect of its inventory turnover ratio and days sales outstanding (DSO) on its cash flow cycle. Christie's 2023 sales (all on credit) were $150,000; and it earned a net profit of 6%, or $9,000. It turned over its inventory 6 times during the year, and its DSO was 36.5 days. The firm had fixed assets totaling $35,000. Christie's payables deferral period is 40 days. i. Calculate Christie's cash conversion cycle. ii. Assuming Christie holds negligible amounts of cash and marketable securities, calculate its total assets turnover and ROA. iii. Suppose Christie's managers believe that the inventory turnover can be raised to 7.3 times. What would Christie's cash conversion cycle, total assets turnover, and ROA have been if the inventory turnover had been 7.3 for 2023? [07] (a) If two mutually exclusive projects were being compared, would a high cost of capital favor the longer-term or the shorter-term project? Why? If the cost of capital declined, would that lead firms to invest more in longer-term projects or shorter-term projects? Would a decline (or an increase) in the WACC cause changes in the IRR ranking of mutually exclusive projects? Explain. [04] (b) An electric utility is considering a new power plant in Chattogram. Power from the plant would be sold in the Hathazari area, where it is badly needed. Because the firm has received a permit, the plant would be legal, but it would cause some air pollution. The company could spend an additional Tk 40 million at Year 0 to mitigate the environmental problem, but it would not be required to do so. The plant without mitigation would cost Tk 240 million, and the expected cash inflows would be Tk 80 million per year for 5 years. If the firm does invest in mitigation, the annual inflows would be Tk 84 million. Unemployment in the area where the plant would be built is high, and the plant would provide about 350 good jobs. The risk-adjusted WACC is 17%. i. Calculate the NPV and IRR with and without mitigation. ii. How should the environmental effects be dealt with when evaluating this project? iii. Should this project be undertaken? If so, should the firm do the mitigation? Why or why not? [11] (a) Would it ever be rational for a firm to borrow money in order to pay cash dividends? [02] (b) What is the difference between a stock dividend and a stock split? As a stockholder, would you prefer to see your company declare a 100% stock dividend or a two-for-one split? Assume that either action is feasible. [03] (c) Clifton Inc. is prepared to report the following 2024 income statement (shown in thousands of dollars). Prior to reporting this income statement, the company wants to determine its annual dividend. The company has 320,000 shares of common stock outstanding, and its stock trades at Tk 37 per share. - i. The company had a 25% dividend payout ratio in 2023. If Brooks wants to maintain this payout ratio in 2024, what will be its per-share dividend in 2024? - ii. If the company maintains this 25% payout ratio, what will be the current dividend yield on the company's stock? - iii. The company reported net income of Tk 1.35 million in 2023. Assume that the number of shares outstanding has remained constant. What was the company's per-share dividend in 2023? - iv. As an alternative to maintaining the same dividend payout ratio, Brooks is considering maintaining the same per-share dividend in 2024 that it paid in 2023. If it chooses this policy, what will be the company's dividend payout ratio in 2024? [10]Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) "The profit maximization is not an operationally feasible criterion." Do you agree? Illustrate your views. Assuming wealth maximization to be the objective of financial management, show how the financing, investment and dividend decisions of a company can help to attain this objective. [07] (b) Why is it necessary for business students who do not plan to major in finance to understand the basics of finance? [04] (c) What do you mean by agency problem? What are some mechanisms that encourage managers to act in the best interests of stockholders? [04] (a) Explain the concept of systematic and unsystematic risk. How can an investor mitigate unsystematic risk? [04] (b) Explain the Capital Market Line (CML) and its significance in the context of the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM). [04] (c) Stocks A and B have the following probability distributions of expected future returns: Data:Required: - I. Calculate the expected rate of return, , for Stock B (.) - II. Calculate the standard deviation of expected returns for Stock A (That for Stock B is 20.35 percent.) Now calculate the coefficient of variation for Stock B. Is it possible that most investors might regard Stock B as being less risky than Stock A? Explain. [07] (a) Discuss why the cost of capital is considered the minimum required rate of return on an investment. How does it influence a firm's investment decisions? [03] (b) Explain the impact of a company's capital structure on its overall cost of capital. How does the mix of debt and equity financing influence this cost? [03] (c) Longstreet Communications Inc. (LCI) has the following capital structure, which it considers to be optimal: debt = 25%, preferred stock = 15%, and common stock = 60%. LCI's tax rate is 40%, and investors expect earnings and dividends to grow at a constant rate of 6% in the future. LCI paid a dividend of $3.70 per share last year (D0), and its stock currently sells at a price of $60 per share. Ten-year Treasury bonds yield 6%, the market risk premium is 5%, and LCI's beta is 1.3. The following terms would apply to new security offerings. Preferred: New preferred could be sold to the public at a price of $100 per share, with a dividend of $9. Flotation costs of $5 per share would be incurred. Debt: Debt could be sold at an interest rate of 9%. Common: New common equity will be raised only by retaining earnings. Required: - I. Find the component costs of debt, preferred stock, and common stock. - II. What is the WACC? [09] (a) Discuss the operating cycle and the cash conversion cycle. How do these cycles affect a company's liquidity and working capital requirements? [03] (b) Compare and contrast aggressive, conservative, and moderate working capital policies. What are the risks and benefits associated with each policy? [04] (c) The board of directors of Aravind mills limited request you to prepare a statement showing the working capital requirements for a level of activity of 30,000 units of output for the year. The cost structure for the company's product for the above-mentioned activity level is given below. Data:Additional Information: - I. Past experience indicates that raw materials are held in stock, on an average for 2 months. - II. Work in progress (100% complete in regard to materials and 50% for labour and overheads) will be half a month's production. - III. Finished goods are in stock on an average for 1 month. - IV. Credit allowed to suppliers: 1 month. - V. Credit allowed to debtors: 2 months. - VI. A minimum cash balance of Rs 25,000 is expected to be maintained.Required: Prepare a statement of working capital requirements. [08] (a) Explain the concept of mutually exclusive projects. How should a firm decide between two mutually exclusive projects? [03] (b) Why is NPV considered a superior method for evaluating capital investment projects? [03] (c) Mr. Solaiman is responsible for considering two investment projects for his firm, each of which requires an up-front expenditure of Tk 25 million. You estimate that the cost of capital is 10% and that the investments will produce the following after-tax cash flows (in millions of taka): Data:Required: - I. What is the regular payback period for each of the projects? - II. What is the discounted payback period for each of the projects? - III. If the two projects are independent and the cost of capital is 10%, which project or projects should the firm undertake? - IV. If the two projects are mutually exclusive and the cost of capital is 5%, which project should the firm undertake? - V. If the two projects are mutually exclusive and the cost of capital is 15%, which project should the firm undertake? - VI. What is the crossover rate? [09] (a) Define optimal capital structure. Briefly outline the four primary factors that influence the capital structure decisions. [05] (b) Briefly explain the (i) MM theory; (ii) Trade-off theory; and (iii) the Signaling theory. [05] (c) The Weaver Watch Company sells watches for $25, the fixed costs are $140,000, and variable costs are $15 per watch. i) What is the breakeven point? Illustrate by means of a chart. ii) What would happen to the breakeven point if the selling price was raised to $31? What is the significance of this analysis? [05] Write Notes on: (i) Business risk and its determinants (ii) Operating leverage (iii) Stand-alone and portfolio risk and their measures (iv) Factors influencing dividend policy (v) Weighted average cost of capital. [15] Tracking Ref: ACC 302 / FCC 209 | BBA 5th Semester 2021 (a) Define financial management. Why is it necessary for business students who do not plan to major in finance to understand the basics of finance? [05] (b) "The ultimate goal of a business firm is to maximize wealth, not to maximize profit." Explain the statement logically. [05] (c) What do you mean by agency problem? What are some mechanisms that encourage managers to act in the best interests of stockholders? [05] (a) Define risk. Distinguish between business risk and financial risk. [04] (b) In general, can the riskiness of a portfolio be reduced to zero by increasing the number of stocks in the portfolio? Explain. [03] (c) Intex corporation is considering three possible capital projects for the next year. Each project has a 1year life and project returns depend on next year's state of the economy. The estimated rates of return are shown in the table: Also assume that Intex Corporation is going to invest one-third of its available funds in each project. Intex corporation will create a portfolio of three equally weighted projects. - i. Find each project's expected rate of return, variance and standard deviation. - ii. What is the expected rate of return, variance and standard deviation of the three project's portfolio? [08] (a) Which method of calculating the cost of equity shares would be most appropriate for the following firms: [04] i. A profitable firm that has never paid a dividend, but has had steady growth in earnings. ii. An electricity company that has paid a dividend every year for the last eighty years. (b) Two firm, F-1 and F-2. The firm F-1 has no debt and is totally financed by equity capital. The firm F-2 has Tk 2,000,000 outstanding debt and pays an interest rate of 10%. The firm's net income after-taxes are calculated using three tax rates, 0, 25 and 50 percent and the resulting values of net incomes are compared. Assume that the earnings before interest and taxes of both firms is Tk 1,000,000 each. Calculate cost of debt. [07] (c) Robi is currently selling for Tk 60 a share. The firm is expected to earn Tk 5.40 per share this year and to pay a year-end dividend of Tk 3.60. i. If investors require a 9 percent return, what rate of growth must be expected for Robi? ii. If Robi reinvests retained earnings in projects whose average return is equal to the stock's expected rate of return, what will be next year's EPS? [Hint: g = (1-Payout rate)(ROE).] [04] (a) Define working capital and working capital management. Discuss the significance of working capital management policy in case of a manufacturing enterprise. [06] (b) From the following information extracted from the books of Zahin Textile Ltd compute the operating cycle in days and the amount of working capital required: (a) What is profitability index? Which one is the superior ranking criterion, profitability index (PI) or net present value (NPV)? Explain. [04] (b) Edelman Engineering is considering including two pieces of equipment, a truck and an overhead pulley system, in this year's capital budget. The projects are independent. The cash outlay for the truck is $17,100, and that for the pulley system is $22,430. The firm's cost of capital is 14%. After-tax cash flows, including depreciation, are as follows: Calculate the IRR, the NPV, and the MIRR for each project, and indicate the correct accept/reject decision for each. [07] (c) Explain why, if two mutually exclusive projects are being compared, the short term project might have the higher ranking under the NPV criterion if the cost of capital is high, but the long-term project might be deemed better if the cost of capital is low. Would changes in the cost of capital ever cause a change in the IRR ranking of two such projects? [04] (a) Explain the logic of the residual dividend model, the steps a firm would take to implement it, and why it is more likely to be used to establish a long-run payout target than to set the actual year-by-year payout ratio.
