Prepare a schedule showing the employer's total cost of salaries and wages for November by function. ii. Prepare the journal entries to record the factory, sales, and administrative payrolls including the employer's payroll taxes. [03] (c) The following are selected 2015 transactions of Darby Corporation. Required: i. Prepare journal entries for the selected transactions above. ii. Prepare adjusting entries at December 31. iii. Compute the total net liability to be reported on the December 31 statement of financial position for: (I) The interest-bearing note; (II) The zero-interest-bearing note. [06] (d) Chen Company has been operating for several years, and on December 31, 2015, presented the following statement of financial position (amounts in thousands). CHEN COMPANYStatement of Financial PositionDecember 31, 2015The net income for 2015 was $25,000. Assume that total assets are the same in 2014 and 2015.Required: Compute each of the following ratios. For each of the four, indicate the manner in which it is computed and its significance as a tool in the analysis of the financial soundness of the company: (i) Current ratio; (ii) Debt to assets; (iii) Acid-test ratio; (iv) Return on assets. Cash dividends were declared and paid during the year. Ordinary shares were issued in exchange for land. Equity investments that cost $35,000 were sold during the year. There were no write-offs of uncollectible accounts during the year. Required: (a) Compare and contrast the direct method and the indirect method for reporting cash flows from operating activities. item.title: Semester Syllabus Mapping
item.description: How to use this note This document maps your 5 courses to the specific textbooks provided. Use the tables to guide your daily reading. Chapters & Sections to Read: Tells you exactly which heading/lesson to focus on. Omit / Skip: Tells you what to ignore so you don't waste time on irrelevant material (e.g., US-specific tax laws, matrix algebra, complex appendices). (Note: ACC 302 does not have a skip list per your instructor's guidance). Local Supplements: Indicates where you need to rely on your professor's class notes or local Bangladeshi laws. Core Textbook: Intermediate Accounting by Kieso, Weygandt, Warfield Syllabus Coverage: ~90%US GAAP vs. IFRS The textbook heavily references US GAAP/FASB. Always focus on the underlying accounting mechanics and skip any sections explicitly detailing LIFO (banned under IFRS) or US tax codes. Core Textbooks: Principles of Managerial Finance by Gitman & Zutter Fundamentals of Financial Management by Van Horne & Wachowicz Fundamentals of Financial Management by Eugene F. Brigham Instructor's Instruction: Read Entirely As per your instructor, do not skip appendices or end-of-chapter sections for the mapped chapters. Read them entirely to get the full depth of the theories, mathematical models, and case studies. How to juggle 3 textbooks Reading 3 books cover-to-cover is time-consuming. Use the "Primary Book" recommended below as your base reading. Once you finish a chapter in the primary book, skim the corresponding chapters in the other two books to catch any additional formulas, examples, or alternative explanations. Core Textbooks: Basic Econometrics by Gujarati AND Research Methodology by Kothari Syllabus Coverage: 100%Textbook Split Topics 1-5 belong to classical statistics (Kothari). Topics 6-10 belong to Econometrics/Regression (Gujarati). Core Textbook: Cost Accounting: A Managerial Emphasis by Horngren, Datar, Rajan Syllabus Coverage: ~80%Missing Content Alert Horngren does not cover the historical Incentive Wage Plans (Taylor, Merrick, Gantt, etc.) or Bangladesh Cost Accounting Standards (BCAS). You must use local books (e.g., Jain & Narang or Polimeni) for Topic 5 wage plans. Core Textbooks: Auditing and Assurance Services by Messier (Foreign) & Contemporary Auditing by Mahmud & Uddin (Local) Syllabus Coverage: 100%Hybrid Study Strategy Use Messier (Foreign): For clear definitions, understanding core logic (like how the Audit Risk Model works), and visualizing business process workflows (Revenue, Inventory, etc.). Use Local Book: For memorizing the specific clauses of the Companies Act 1994, the ICAB Code of Ethics, and the exact structures of ISAs (International Standards on Auditing) required by your syllabus.

item.title: PYQ Final 2025
item.description:
(a) Construct your own definition of 'risk' and justify the conceptual boundary between risk and uncertainty.
(b) Justify the necessity of risk management in contemporary business operations. Identify at least four common organisational risks and outline the sequential stages of an effective risk management framework.
(c) Contrast pure risk with speculative risk using real-life scenarios. Show how the element of loss operates differently in each category. For each of the following risk situations, design an appropriate risk management strategy (single or combination) and defend your choice:
(a) Rahim, a 45-year-old bank manager, has a sedentary lifestyle and his father died of a heart attack at age 55.
(b) A private investment fund notices unusual volatility in the stock market that threatens its portfolio value.
(c) A software development firm discovers critical security loopholes in its client database system.
(d) A small business owner fears bankruptcy because of mounting personal loan obligations.
(e) A garment export company has three factories located in coastal areas frequently hit by cyclones and tidal surges.
(a) Explain the interrelationship between loss frequency and loss severity in risk assessment. Use examples to show how a change in one can impact the other.
(b) How can quantitative methods like probability distributions and statistical analysis be used to assess loss frequency and severity? Illustrate with an example.
(c) Discuss how changes in economic conditions such as inflation and interest rates affect the demand for insurance among individuals and organisations.
(a) Distinguish between insurance and gambling. Illustrate your answer with suitable examples, and explain why insurance is generally regarded as a socially beneficial practice, whereas gambling is not.
(b) Explain the principle of utmost good faith in insurance contracts. Why is this principle essential for maintaining trust and fairness between the insurer and the insured?
(c) Discuss the significance of the principle of "insurable interest" in insurance contracts. Illustrate your answer with suitable examples.
(d) Discuss the purpose and importance of reinsurance in the insurance industry. Explain how reinsurance enables insurance companies to manage their risk exposure effectively.
(a) Craft a precise definition of life insurance and highlight its primary mission. Show how life insurance serves as a tool for intergenerational financial security.
(b) Contrast term life, whole life, and universal life insurance on parameters such as premium structure, cash value, and suitability for different life stages.
(c) Identify the pressing challenges confronting the life insurance industry today and examine recent trends including insurtech innovations and evolving consumer expectations.
(a) Explain the concept of marine insurance and discuss its significance in international trade. Illustrate your answer with suitable examples.
(b) Discuss the key elements of a marine insurance policy. Define the following types of marine insurance policies: i. Time Policy ii. Unvalued Policy iii. Floating Policy iv. Blanket Policy v. Block Policy
(a) Enumerate and briefly characterise the diverse life insurance product categories currently operated and administered by Jiban Bima Corporation.
(b) Compose a concise analytical note on the establishment, mandate, and key functions of the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority (IDRA) of Bangladesh.
(c) Propose a set of actionable policy measures and strategic initiatives that the Government of Bangladesh ought to adopt in order to enhance the public appeal and penetration of the insurance business.
(a) Define ethics. Identify the relationship between ethics and law.
(b) Briefly explain the importance of business ethics.
(c) Point out the relevance of globalisation for business ethics.
(a) Explain the key components of an ethical decision in business. How do individual factors, such as moral development, personal values, and cognitive biases, influence ethical decision-making?
(b) Define Sustainability and explain how the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework shifts the goal of a corporation from purely economic value to an extended set of social and environmental goals.
(c) A Bangladeshi tea estate owner finds that using a specific pesticide increases yield by 30% but is contaminating into local water sources used by villagers. Using the TBL framework, argue why the owner should or should not continue using the pesticide. Consider the economic benefits, social impacts, and environmental consequences in your answer.
(a) Discuss the ethical issues that arise in the firm-employee relationship. How does globalisation create additional ethical challenges for companies employing people in developing countries?
(b) Outline the core rights and duties of employees in an organisation. How does workplace discrimination violate these rights?
(c) FoodGiant is a large food and beverage company. In developing countries, it advertises sugary foods and drinks to children using cartoon characters, free toys, and school programmes. However, in developed countries, the company promotes its own products as healthy choices. At the same time, workers in FoodGiant's factories work 12 hours a day without extra pay for overtime. Employees who try to form a labour union often lose their jobs. Required: i. Identify the ethical issues related to FoodGiant's treatment of consumers and employees. ii. Explain why the company's marketing practices in developing countries can be considered a double standard. iii. Discuss whether FoodGiant's actions are socially responsible. Support your answer with reasons.
(a) Define business ethics management. Explain its components.
(b) Briefly explain the different types of ethical codes.
(c) Identify the reasons for social accounting by the organisations.
(a) How does the government function as a stakeholder in business ethics? What ethical issues typically arise in the relationship between business and government, particularly in developing economies?
(b) What is meant by 'corporate citizenship'? Discuss the relationship between viewing a business as a "key player in the regulatory game" versus a "passive rule-follower". How should corporations engage with government in an ethical manner?
(c) MegaPort Ltd. is a large port infrastructure company seeking a major government contract in a South Asian country. Company representatives paid government officials a fee to accelerate the approval process, although illegal under international anti-bribery laws. This is a common local practice. The company argues that without such payments, it cannot compete with the local firms who routinely engage in such practices. Also, it claims that the project will bring thousands of jobs and local people. Required: Analyze the ethical dimensions of MegaPort Ltd.'s conduct using the concepts of government as stakeholder, corporate citizenship, and globalisation of business-government relations. Is the 'common local practice' argument ethically valid? What systemic changes in both corporate governance and regulatory frameworks would help prevent such ethical violations?
(a) Explain the Agency Relationship between shareholders (principals) and managers (agents), identifying the roles of conflict of interest and informational asymmetry.
(b) A large multinational company seeks a hostile takeover of a traditional Bangladeshi food brand without the board's approval. Evaluate the potential impact of this takeover on employee welfare and local community identity.
(c) In a major Bangladeshi pharmaceutical firm, the CEO sold a significant volume of personal shares in the company one week before the public announcement of a failed drug trial that caused the stock price to fall by 35%. The information about the drug trial failure was known internally months before the announcement. Minority shareholders suffered major losses. Regulators launched an investigation, but the CEO argued the sale was 'planned in advance' for personal financial reasons. Required: Analyze the above case from the perspectives of (i) ethical issues in corporate governance, (ii) shareholder rights. What governance reforms should the company implement to prevent such a situation?
(a) Distinguish between Consequentialist and Non-consequentialist ethical theories. Provide one business example for each to illustrate their application.
(b) Compare and contrast egoism, Utilitarianism, and ethics of duties. Which theory do you consider most applicable to modern business decision-making and why?
(c) Nadia is the operations director of a garment factory in Chittagong. Year-end profits are strong. She faces a choice: (1) distribute a substantial bonus to all 500 workers, improving their living standards but reducing investor dividends; or (2) pay higher dividends to shareholders to retain investment for planned expansion, which may create 200 new jobs next year but provides nothing to current workers now. Some senior managers suggest a third path: allocate funds to improve safety equipment, which satisfies no one immediately but reduces accident risk in future periods. Required: Apply at least two ethical theories to evaluate each of Nadia's three options. Which course of action is most ethically defensible? Justify your reasoning.
(a) Passion works as a driving force for a successful entrepreneur. Elucidate the statement by defining Entrepreneur and Entrepreneurship.
(b) Define execution intelligence. How would you relate it with an entrepreneur?
(c) Mention some attributes of firms that pursue high levels of corporate entrepreneurship.
(d) In 1978, Ayesha Abed helped establish Aarong in Bangladesh to create sustainable income opportunities for rural artisans, especially women. At that time, many artisans struggled to find reliable markets for their handcrafted products and often faced delayed payments. Ayesha Abed recognized this problem and transformed it into an entrepreneurial opportunity by connecting rural producers with urban consumers through Aarong. Her success demonstrates several key entrepreneurial qualities. First, she showed vision by identifying an unmet market need. Second, she displayed leadership by organising thousands of artisans into a productive network. Third, she exhibited social responsibility, ensuring fair prices and employment opportunities for disadvantaged women. Finally, her perseverance and innovation helped Aarong grow from a small outlet into one of Bangladesh's leading lifestyle retail brands. Today, Aarong supports tens of thousands of artisans and serves as a successful example of how entrepreneurial qualities can create both business success and positive social impact in Bangladesh. Required: i) Which entrepreneurial quality was most important in establishing Aarong? Why? ii) How did leadership contribute to Aarong's success? iii) In what way did Aarong create social value in Bangladesh?
(a) How can finding a gap in the marketplace create a business opportunity for an entrepreneur to pursue?
(b) How does creativity contribute to the opportunity recognition process?
(c) Point out some traits that help an entrepreneur in successful opportunity recognition.
(d) In many areas of coastal Bangladesh, especially in districts such as Satkhira and Khulna, people face severe shortages of safe drinking water due to salinity in groundwater. During the dry season, families often travel long distances to collect fresh water, which consumes time and affects health and productivity. Recognising this problem, Drinkwell introduced community-based water purification systems that convert saline and contaminated water into safe drinking water. The company installs purification plants in villages and operates them through local entrepreneurs. Residents can purchase clean water at an affordable price while local operators earn income from managing the facilities. This solution addressed a significant social problem while creating a sustainable business opportunity. As a result, thousands of people gained access to safe drinking water, waterborne diseases were reduced, and local employment opportunities were created. The case demonstrates how identifying a community problem can lead to innovative entrepreneurial ventures that generate both social and economic value. Required: i) What problem did Drinkwell identify in coastal Bangladesh? ii) Why can this case be considered an entrepreneurial opportunity? iii) What innovation did the company introduce?
(a) What is the best time for a firm to develop its business model?
(b) Pathao, one of Bangladesh's leading digital platforms, emerged in 2015 as a motorcycle-based ride-sharing service at a time when Dhaka's traffic congestion was among the worst in the world. Traditional transportation—taxis, rickshaws, and buses—struggled to offer reliability or speed. Pathao introduced a disruptive business model built on smartphone connectivity, real-time matching, and a gig-based rider network. Instead of owning vehicles, Pathao empowered thousands of freelance bikers to join the platform, drastically lowering operational costs and enabling rapid scale-up. Pathao further expanded into food delivery, courier services, and digital payments through Pathao Pay, creating a multi-sided digital ecosystem. Each service disrupted a separate traditional sector: restaurant deliveries, parcel logistics, and even cash-based transactions. Its pricing transparency, quick service, and user-friendly app attracted a large urban young population, while conventional transport operators and courier companies faced declining demand and competitive pressure. By leveraging local market insights—such as acceptance of mobile payments and the widespread use of affordable smartphones—Pathao adapted global ride-sharing concepts to Bangladeshi realities. The company's disruptive approach not only redefined urban mobility but also generated income opportunities for tens of thousands of riders and delivery agents, reshaping Bangladesh's digital economy. Required: i) What made Pathao's business model disruptive in Bangladesh? ii) Which traditional industries were most affected by Pathao's expansion? iii) What local factors enabled Pathao's success in the Bangladeshi market?
(c) Briefly point out the main contents of a business plan.
(d) In 2022, three graduates from Chattogram noticed that many farmers in rural Bangladesh struggled to sell fresh vegetables at fair prices because of multiple intermediaries. At the same time, urban consumers often paid high prices for vegetables that were not always fresh. Seeing this gap, the entrepreneurs developed a business plan for Aamra Fresh Agro, a startup that would connect farmers directly with consumers through a mobile app and delivery network. The business plan included a market analysis showing increasing demand for safe and fresh food in major cities such as Dhaka and Chattogram. The founders estimated an initial investment of BDT 15 lakh for app development, cold-storage facilities, and delivery vehicles. Revenue would come from a commission on each sale and subscription packages for regular customers. The plan identified potential risks, including transportation delays, seasonal fluctuations in production, and competition from established online grocery platforms. To address these challenges, the entrepreneurs planned partnerships with local farmer cooperatives and logistics providers. They also projected that the business would break even within three years if monthly sales grew by 10%. After presenting the business plan to investors, the startup secured seed funding and launched operations. Within the first year, it supplied fresh vegetables to more than 2,000 households and increased participating farmers' incomes by approximately 20%. Required: i) What were the main sources of revenue for Aamra Fresh Agro? ii) What risks were identified in the business plan?
(a) What are the prerequisites for building a strong ethical culture in a firm?
(b) Define the concept liability of newness. What can a new venture do to overcome the liability of newness?
(c) Why does having relevant industry experience help the founder of a firm to be successful?
(d) FreshBrew is a mobile coffee truck business started by college friends Mia and Arif. They noticed many commuters near their city's business district lacked quick access to quality coffee. After securing a small investor, they launched the truck and hired an assistant manager. Although they had a great product, the business struggled. Customers sometimes waited too long, and social media feedback was slow. Mia realised that they needed more help with operations and marketing to grow. They also felt inexperienced running a business and had no credible reputation with suppliers yet. Mia and Arif invited two industry advisors with café experience to join their team to help with training and supplier contracts. Required: i. What concept explains FreshBrew's early struggles because the founders lacked experience and reputation? ii. Why might adding industry advisors help FreshBrew? iii. What is the benefit of having more than one founder or team member?
(a) Define acquisition with an example. Why do acquisitions fail sometimes?
(b) What challenges do second-generation entrepreneurs face when taking over established family business?
(c) Amena Akter, a resident of Cumilla, started a small online clothing business in 2019. She sold traditional Bangladeshi dresses through social media and initially operated from her home with a small amount of personal savings. Her products gained popularity among local customers, and she planned to expand her business by opening a boutique and hiring employees. However, Amena faced several challenges common to many women entrepreneurs in Bangladesh. One major challenge was limited access to finance. Banks often required collateral and lengthy documentation, which made it difficult for her to obtain a business loan. She also encountered social barriers, as some family and community members believed that women should prioritise household responsibilities over business activities. Another challenge was balancing family and business commitments. As a mother of two children, Amena had to manage household duties while handling customer orders, supplier negotiations, and marketing activities. Additionally, she faced difficulties in building professional networks, which are often crucial for obtaining business information and opportunities. The COVID-19 pandemic further disrupted her business by reducing customer demand and creating supply-chain problems. Despite these obstacles, Amena adapted by increasing her online marketing efforts, offering home delivery services, and participating in entrepreneurship training programmes organised by local support organisations. Today, her business employs six women and serves customers across Bangladesh. Amena's story demonstrates both the significant challenges faced by women entrepreneurs and their ability to overcome barriers through resilience, innovation, and determination. Required: i) What financial challenge did Amena face? ii) What social barrier affected her business growth? iii) How did family responsibilities impact her entrepreneurship? iv) What strategies helped her overcome challenges?
(a) Identify the keys to effective new product development. Explain the common reasons new products fail.
(b) Explain the difference between internal growth strategies and external growth strategies.
(c) Explain "licensing" and how it can be used as a growth strategy.
(a) Explain why most new ventures need to raise money at some point during their early life?
(b) Identify the three steps involved in properly preparing to raise debt or equity financing.
(c) Explain why an initial public offering is an important milestone for a firm.
(d) Explain the advantages of leasing for an entrepreneurial firm.
(a) Define organisational behaviour. What is the importance of interpersonal skills in the workplace?
(b) Describe the major behavioural science disciplines that contribute to Organisational Behaviour.
(c) Why might the same Organisational Behaviour concept succeed in one organisation but fail in another? Analyze using any two challenges and two opportunities managers face in applying Organisational Behaviour concepts.
(a) A software company needs to hire for a programming role, while a construction company needs to hire for a heavy equipment operator role. Analyse which type of ability (intellectual or physical) is more critical for each role and why.
(b) What are biographical characteristics? Identify and explain how they affect Organisational Behaviour.
(c) What causes job satisfaction? Compare the relative importance of pay versus the work itself.
(a) What are the three components of attitude? How can managers use an understanding of attitudes to predict employee behaviour?
(b) What is Emotional Labour? Distinguish between surface acting and deep acting with examples from a customer service job.
(c) GreenMart Superstore employs a large team of cashiers and customer service representatives. In the past six months, management noticed rising absenteeism, customer complaints, and employee turnover. Exit interviews revealed employees felt unappreciated, emotionally exhausted, and dissatisfied with their work. Several employees stated they had to 'fake smiles' all day despite dealing with rude customers and heavy workloads. Required: i. Which major job attitudes—job satisfaction, organisational commitment, or employee engagement—seem most affected at GreenMart? Explain with reference to the case. ii. How can the concept of Emotional Intelligence (EI) help GreenMart's supervisors reduce employee burnout and improve morale?
(a) Briefly describe the Big Five Personality Model. Which trait do you think is most important for a manager in Bangladesh's business environment? Justify your answer.
(b) What is perception? Explain any three common perceptual shortcuts (biases) that managers should be aware of when evaluating employees.
(c) What is the link between perception and individual decision making? How can organisational constraints affect decisions?
(a) What is a group? Explain the stages of group development in your own words.
(b) What is the difference between a work group and a work team? What are the key characteristics of an effective team?
(c) BDCom Networks formed a cross-functional project team to develop a new billing system. The team consists of members from IT, Finance, and Customer Service departments. In the first few weeks, members were polite but uncertain about roles. By the second month, open conflicts arose over who should lead. Members from different departments argued about priorities, and the project fell behind schedule. Required: i. At which stage of group development is this team currently? Justify your answer using evidence from the case. ii. As the team leader, suggest two specific actions you would take to move the team to the 'Norming' or 'Performing' stage.
(a) Why is leadership important in organisations? Briefly distinguish between charismatic leadership and transformational leadership.
(b) Define power. What are the five bases of power explored in the text? Which base of power is most sustainable in the long run, and why?
(c) Mr. X was recently promoted to Factory Manager at DynaFab Ltd. He noticed that several senior workers ignored his instructions but quickly obeyed orders from the previous manager, who had worked at DynaFab for 20 years. Mr. X relies mostly on his formal authority (position) to gain compliance, but the results have been poor. Workers seem to respect only those they consider experienced and trustworthy. Required: i. Which type of power is Mr. X relying on, and which power bases does the previous manager likely possess? Use the case to support your answer. ii. What advice would you give Mr. X to build a more effective power base and gain genuine influence over his team?
(a) Define conflict. Explain the five stages of the conflict process as described in the textbook.
(b) What is organisational change? What are the most common reasons employees resist change? Suggest two ways managers can overcome resistance.
(c) MegaBank recently merged with a smaller bank. Following the merger, employees experienced role ambiguity, fear of job loss, increased workloads, and poor communication from management. Many employees began reporting headaches, insomnia, and reduced concentration. Absenteeism rose by 30%. A group of senior tellers refused to adopt the new software system, causing operational delays. Required: i. Identify at least two sources of stress (organisational and personal) that MegaBank employees are experiencing. What consequences of stress are visible in this case? ii. As an HR consultant, recommend one individual-level and one organisational-level strategy to help MegaBank manage stress effectively during this change.
(a) Write a brief on the history of Bangladesh mentioning Pakistan movement and the birth of Pakistan, language movement (1948-1952), Juktafront election of 1954, six points programme of 1966, mass upsurge of 1969, election of 1970 and birth of Bangladesh in 1971.
(b) What do you know about the constitution of Bangladesh? Discuss the features of constitution-1972 of people's republic of Bangladesh.
(c) Discuss the judiciary system of Bangladesh.
(a) Discuss the characteristics of Bangladesh economy. What are the reasons for underdevelopment of Bangladesh?
(b) Mention the main cottage industries in Bangladesh. What role small and cottage industries can play for a developing country like Bangladesh?
(c) What are the features of the population of Bangladesh? Discuss the impact of overpopulation on the Bangladesh economy.
(a) Is economic development means economic growth? How can you measure the Human Development Index (HDI)? Briefly discuss the factors that determine economic growth.
(b) Explain the Kuznets hypothesis of economic growth and income distribution. What are the causes of increase in income inequality with economic development?
(c) What do you mean by sustainable development? Briefly discuss the sustainable development goals.
(a) What is poverty? Discuss the poverty alleviation programme of different organisations in Bangladesh.
(b) Write a brief on the 8th five-year plan of Bangladesh.
(c) What do you mean by micro credit? Do you think that microcredit programme can reduce poverty in Bangladesh? Discuss the major activities of NGOs.
(a) What drives economic development according to Schumpeter? Discuss the salient features of Schumpeter model of economic development.
(b) What is the big push theory? Why is big push needed in a less developed country?
(c) Discuss the theories of balanced and unbalanced growth. Which model do you support to be applicable for developing countries like Bangladesh?
(a) How capital formation can be a measure of economic development of Bangladesh? Discuss the sources of capital formation.
(b) Discuss the theory of demographic transition in economic development with criticism. Bangladesh in what part of this theory?
(c) "A strong agricultural economy brings social progress" – Do you agree? Explain your view.
(a) Give a comparison between developed and developing countries. What lessons do you learn from developed countries for Bangladesh?
(b) Discuss the traditional theory of free trade with regard to its effects on a country's development.
(c) What measures encourage economic integration among developing countries? Discuss the benefits from and problems of economic integration.

item.title: Syllabus Mapping
item.description: How to use this note This document maps your 5 courses to the specific textbooks provided. Use the tables to guide your daily reading. Chapters & Sections to Read: Tells you exactly which heading/lesson to focus on. Omit / Skip: Tells you what to ignore so you don't waste time on irrelevant material (e.g., US-specific tax laws, matrix algebra, complex appendices). Local Supplements: Indicates where you need to rely on your professor's class notes or local Bangladeshi laws. Core Textbook: Intermediate Accounting by Kieso, Weygandt, Warfield Syllabus Coverage: ~90%US GAAP vs. IFRS The textbook heavily references US GAAP/FASB. Always focus on the underlying accounting mechanics and skip any sections explicitly detailing LIFO (banned under IFRS) or US tax codes. Core Textbook: Principles of Managerial Finance by Gitman and Zutter Syllabus Coverage: ~85%Core Textbooks: Basic Econometrics by Gujarati AND Research Methodology by Kothari Syllabus Coverage: 100%Textbook Split Topics 1-5 belong to classical statistics (Kothari). Topics 6-10 belong to Econometrics/Regression (Gujarati). Core Textbook: Cost Accounting: A Managerial Emphasis by Horngren, Datar, Rajan Syllabus Coverage: ~80%Missing Content Alert Horngren does not cover the historical Incentive Wage Plans (Taylor, Merrick, Gantt, etc.) or Bangladesh Cost Accounting Standards (BCAS). You must use local books (e.g., Jain & Narang or Polimeni) for Topic 5 wage plans. Core Textbook: Auditing and Assurance Services by Messier, Glover, Prawitt Syllabus Coverage: ~85%Approach to Auditing Do not memorize the textbook word-for-word. Focus on the core logic: Why are we testing this? Which management assertion does this test prove?

item.title: PYQ ACC 302
item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester Standard Format: 4 Hours | 75 Marks | Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially.Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) "Investment, financing and dividend decisions are all interrelated." Comment. [03] (b) "To avoid the problem of shortage and surplus of funds, what is required in Financial management? Name the concept and explain four points of importance. [04] (c) Explain why the following statements appearing in the objectives of two well-known listed companies are not necessarily contradictory? [04] "We never confuse why we exist - to create the maximum possible returns to our shareholders." "In everything the company does, it is committed to creating wealth always with integrity, for our employees, customers, suppliers and the community in which we operate." (d) Why do managers and other agents of the shareholders, such as employees sometimes have different objectives? [04] (a) Explain the following statement: "Most investors are risk averse." [03] (b) "An asset held as part of a portfolio is generally less risky than the same asset held in isolation." Do you agree with this statement? Why or why not? [03] (c) BSCCL stock has an expected return of 10 percent, a beta coefficient of 0.9, and a standard deviation of expected returns of 35 percent. BSC stock has an expected return of 12.5 percent, a beta coefficient of 1.2, and a standard deviation of expected returns of 25 percent. The risk-free rate is 6 percent, and the market risk premium is 5 percent. i. Calculate each stock's coefficient of variation. ii. Which stock is riskier for diversified investors? iii. Calculate each stock's required rate of return. iv. On the basis of the two stocks' expected and required returns, which stock would be most attractive to a diversified investor? v. Calculate the required return of a portfolio that has tk. 7,500 invested in BSCCL stock and tk. 2,500 invested in BSC stock. vi. If the market risk premium increased to 6 percent, which of the two stocks would have the largest increase in their required return? [09] (a) Assume that there are three stocks in a portfolio- stock-1, stock-2, and stock-3. The expected return vector of this portfolio is and the weighting vector of this portfolio is where, The variances of stock-1, stock-2, and stock-3 are 12%, 7%, and 9% respectively and the correlation coefficients between stock-1 and stock-2, stock-1 and stock-3, and stock-2 and stock-3 are 0.2, -0.6, and -0.3. Required: i. Compute portfolio return (use vector multiplication). [02] ii. Compute portfolio risk (use vector multiplication). [07] iii. Compute minimum and maximum portfolio return. [02] (b) A firm's equity beta is 0.9. The risk-free rate is 4% and the expected market return is 11%. Calculate the cost of equity. [02] (c) A firm's stock is currently being traded at $40. The expected dividend next year is $2.50 and dividends are expected to grow at 5% per year indefinitely. Estimate the cost of equity capital. [02] (a) A two-year bond has a face value of $1,000 and a coupon rate of 8% paid annually. The probability of default each year is 4%. If default occurs, the recovery value is $500. The bond is issued at par. Estimate the expected cost of debt. [05] (b) A project is fully financed by equity and has the same business risk as three pure-play comparable firms that are also all-equity financed. The equity betas of the comparable firms are 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6, respectively. The risk-free rate is 4% and the market risk premium is 8%. Estimate the appropriate discount rate for the project. [05] (c) How can investors be classified in terms of their risk preference? [05] (a) A firm operates in a perfect capital market where the Modigliani-Miller (MM) assumptions hold and there are no taxes. The firm's overall cost of capital (cost of assets) is 12 percent. The firm is financed with $4 million of debt and $6 million of equity. The cost of debt is 7 percent. Find the cost of equity. [02] (b) An investor owns 1% of an unlevered firm worth $5,000,000. The firm decides to remain unlevered, but the investor wants leverage equivalent to a firm with 40% debt. How can the investor create homemade leverage? [03] (c) A firm is financed with both debt and equity. The market value of debt is $5 million and the market value of equity is also $5 million. The required rate of return on equity is 14 percent, while the cost of debt is 8 percent. The corporate tax rate is 30 percent. In addition, investors face personal taxes: interest income is taxed at 40 percent, whereas equity income is taxed at 20 percent. Find the firm's weighted average cost of capital (WACC) considering both corporate and personal taxes. [05] (d) A firm generates an annual EBIT of $1,200,000. The required return on assets for an unlevered firm is 10 percent. The corporate tax rate is 30 percent. The firm plans to issue permanent debt of $4,000,000. In addition to corporate taxes, investors face personal taxes: Personal tax rate on interest income = 35% Personal tax rate on equity income = 15% Required: i. Find the value of the unlevered firm. [02] ii. Find the value of the levered firm considering both corporate and personal taxes. [03] (a) A company has reported earnings per share of $4.00 and maintains a dividend payout ratio of 40 percent. The company's return on equity is 15 percent, and the required rate of return on the stock is 12 percent. The company is expected to experience high growth for the next four years, after which it will settle into a stable growth rate of 5 percent indefinitely. Estimate the intrinsic value of the stock using the two-stage dividend discount model, where the high-growth rate is derived from the firm's sustainable growth rate. [04] (b) A company issues a $1,000 par bond, paying a 10% annual coupon semiannually for 6 years. The required annual rate of return is 12%. Determine the bond value. [03] (c) An investor purchases one European call option on a stock that is currently trading at $40 per share. The option has a strike price of $35 and a premium of $5, and it expires in three months. Determine the payoff and profit or loss at expiration for various possible stock prices: $30, $35, $40, $45, and $50 and plot the results in the graph. [05] (d) A stock is currently trading at $50. A European call option with a strike price of $55 expiring in 6 months is trading at $4.50, and a European put option with the same strike price and expiration is trading at $9.00. The risk-free interest rate for 6 months is 2% (continuously compounded). Verify whether put-call parity holds and explain the relationship between the call and put prices. [03] A firm is evaluating a proposal to install a new production machine to expand its operations. The project requires careful estimation of cash flows considering depreciation tax shield and interest tax shield.Project Information: Cost of new machine: USD 10,000,000 Installation and transportation cost: USD 1,000,000 Total initial investment: USD 11,000,000 The machine will be depreciated using the straight-line method over 5 years to a salvage value of USD 1,000,000. The project life is 5 years. Operating Information: Expected annual sales revenue: USD 6,000,000 Annual operating costs (excluding depreciation and interest): USD 3,000,000 Corporate tax rate: 30% The project will be financed as follows: 40% debt and 60% equity Loan amount will carry an interest rate of 10% per year The loan will be repaid in equal principal installments over 5 years Additional Information: Expected salvage value at the end of Year 5: USD 1,200,000 Working capital requirement: USD 500,000 (required at the beginning and fully recovered at the end of Year 5) Required rate of return (WACC): 12% Required: i. Estimate the initial cash flows of the project. [1] ii. Estimate the operating cash flows of the project. [5] iii. Estimate the terminal cash flows of the project. [3] iv. Based on the NPV, should the company accept the project? Justify your answer. [6] Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) What are the possible alternative financial goals of the organization? Which one do you recommend and why? [06] (b) Point out the decisions that are made by financial manager. Explain. [05] (c) What do mean by agency costs? How can this costs be minimized? [04] (a) Explain why you agree or disagree with this statement "Most investors are risk-averse". [03] (b) Consider the following information for Stocks A, B, and C. The returns on the three stocks are positively correlated, but they are not perfectly correlated. (That is, each of the correlation coefficients is between 0 and 1.) Fund Dhaka Ltd has one-third of its funds invested in each of the three stocks. The risk-free rate is 5.5%, and the market is in equilibrium. (That is, required returns equal expected returns.) Requirements: - i. What is the market risk premium ()? - ii. What is the beta of Fund Dhaka Ltd? - iii. What is the required return of Fund Dhaka Ltd? - iv. Would you expect the standard deviation of Fund Dhaka Ltd to be less than 15%, equal to 15%, or greater than 15%? Explain. [08] (c) A mutual fund manager has a Tk. 20 million portfolio with a beta of 1.7. The risk-free rate is 4.5%, and the market risk premium is 7%. The manager expects to receive an additional Tk. 5 million, which she plans to invest in a number of stocks. After investing the additional funds, she wants the fund's required return to be 15%. What should be the average beta of the new stocks added to the portfolio? [04] (a) General Electric Company (GEC) uses only debt and common equity. It can borrow unlimited amounts at an interest rate of as long as it finances at its target capital structure, which calls for 35% debt and 65% common equity. Its last dividend () was Tk 2.20, its expected constant growth rate is 6%, and its common stock sells for Tk 26. GEC's tax rate is 40%. Two projects are available: Project A has a rate of return of 12% and Project B's return is 11%. These two projects are equally risky and about as risky as the firm's existing assets. i. What is its cost of common equity? ii. What is the WACC? iii. Which projects should GEC accept? [08] (b) The KR Company's EPS was TK 6.50 in 2024, up from TK 4.42 in 2019. The company pays out 40% of its earnings as dividends, and its common stock sells for TK 36.00. i. Calculate the past growth rate in earnings. (Hint: This is a 5-year growth period.) ii. The last dividend was . Calculate the next expected dividend, , assuming that the past growth rate continues. iii. What is KR's cost of retained earnings, ? [07] (a) Explain this statement "Using financial leverage has both good and bad effects". [03] (b) Explain what asymmetric information means, and how signals affect capital structure decisions. [04] (c) A company currently has assets of Tk 5 million. The firm is 100 percent equity financed. The company currently has net income of Tk 1.5 million, and it pays out 40 percent of its net income as dividends. Both net income and dividends are expected to grow at a constant rate of 6 percent per year. There are 200,000 shares of stock outstanding, and it is estimated that the current cost of capital is 13.40 percent. The company is considering a recapitalization where it will issue Tk 1.5 million in debt and use the proceeds to repurchase stock. Investment bankers have estimated that if the company goes through with the recapitalization, its before-tax cost of debt will be 11 percent, and the cost of equity will rise to 14.5 percent. The company has a 40 percent federal tax rate. i. What is the current share price of the stock (before the recapitalization)? ii. Assuming that the company maintains the same payout ratio, what will be its stock price following the recapitalization? [08] (a) Delineate the alternative current asset financing policies with suitable diagram. [05] (b) What is cash conversion cycle? Define its three components. [03] (c) Christie Corporation is trying to determine the effect of its inventory turnover ratio and days sales outstanding (DSO) on its cash flow cycle. Christie's 2023 sales (all on credit) were $150,000; and it earned a net profit of 6%, or $9,000. It turned over its inventory 6 times during the year, and its DSO was 36.5 days. The firm had fixed assets totaling $35,000. Christie's payables deferral period is 40 days. i. Calculate Christie's cash conversion cycle. ii. Assuming Christie holds negligible amounts of cash and marketable securities, calculate its total assets turnover and ROA. iii. Suppose Christie's managers believe that the inventory turnover can be raised to 7.3 times. What would Christie's cash conversion cycle, total assets turnover, and ROA have been if the inventory turnover had been 7.3 for 2023? [07] (a) If two mutually exclusive projects were being compared, would a high cost of capital favor the longer-term or the shorter-term project? Why? If the cost of capital declined, would that lead firms to invest more in longer-term projects or shorter-term projects? Would a decline (or an increase) in the WACC cause changes in the IRR ranking of mutually exclusive projects? Explain. [04] (b) An electric utility is considering a new power plant in Chattogram. Power from the plant would be sold in the Hathazari area, where it is badly needed. Because the firm has received a permit, the plant would be legal, but it would cause some air pollution. The company could spend an additional Tk 40 million at Year 0 to mitigate the environmental problem, but it would not be required to do so. The plant without mitigation would cost Tk 240 million, and the expected cash inflows would be Tk 80 million per year for 5 years. If the firm does invest in mitigation, the annual inflows would be Tk 84 million. Unemployment in the area where the plant would be built is high, and the plant would provide about 350 good jobs. The risk-adjusted WACC is 17%. i. Calculate the NPV and IRR with and without mitigation. ii. How should the environmental effects be dealt with when evaluating this project? iii. Should this project be undertaken? If so, should the firm do the mitigation? Why or why not? [11] (a) Would it ever be rational for a firm to borrow money in order to pay cash dividends? [02] (b) What is the difference between a stock dividend and a stock split? As a stockholder, would you prefer to see your company declare a 100% stock dividend or a two-for-one split? Assume that either action is feasible. [03] (c) Clifton Inc. is prepared to report the following 2024 income statement (shown in thousands of dollars). Prior to reporting this income statement, the company wants to determine its annual dividend. The company has 320,000 shares of common stock outstanding, and its stock trades at Tk 37 per share. - i. The company had a 25% dividend payout ratio in 2023. If Brooks wants to maintain this payout ratio in 2024, what will be its per-share dividend in 2024? - ii. If the company maintains this 25% payout ratio, what will be the current dividend yield on the company's stock? - iii. The company reported net income of Tk 1.35 million in 2023. Assume that the number of shares outstanding has remained constant. What was the company's per-share dividend in 2023? - iv. As an alternative to maintaining the same dividend payout ratio, Brooks is considering maintaining the same per-share dividend in 2024 that it paid in 2023. If it chooses this policy, what will be the company's dividend payout ratio in 2024? [10]Tracking Ref: ACC 302 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) "The profit maximization is not an operationally feasible criterion." Do you agree? Illustrate your views. Assuming wealth maximization to be the objective of financial management, show how the financing, investment and dividend decisions of a company can help to attain this objective. [07] (b) Why is it necessary for business students who do not plan to major in finance to understand the basics of finance? [04] (c) What do you mean by agency problem? What are some mechanisms that encourage managers to act in the best interests of stockholders? [04] (a) Explain the concept of systematic and unsystematic risk. How can an investor mitigate unsystematic risk? [04] (b) Explain the Capital Market Line (CML) and its significance in the context of the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM). [04] (c) Stocks A and B have the following probability distributions of expected future returns: Data:Required: - I. Calculate the expected rate of return, , for Stock B (.) - II. Calculate the standard deviation of expected returns for Stock A (That for Stock B is 20.35 percent.) Now calculate the coefficient of variation for Stock B. Is it possible that most investors might regard Stock B as being less risky than Stock A? Explain. [07] (a) Discuss why the cost of capital is considered the minimum required rate of return on an investment. How does it influence a firm's investment decisions? [03] (b) Explain the impact of a company's capital structure on its overall cost of capital. How does the mix of debt and equity financing influence this cost? [03] (c) Longstreet Communications Inc. (LCI) has the following capital structure, which it considers to be optimal: debt = 25%, preferred stock = 15%, and common stock = 60%. LCI's tax rate is 40%, and investors expect earnings and dividends to grow at a constant rate of 6% in the future. LCI paid a dividend of $3.70 per share last year (D0), and its stock currently sells at a price of $60 per share. Ten-year Treasury bonds yield 6%, the market risk premium is 5%, and LCI's beta is 1.3. The following terms would apply to new security offerings. Preferred: New preferred could be sold to the public at a price of $100 per share, with a dividend of $9. Flotation costs of $5 per share would be incurred. Debt: Debt could be sold at an interest rate of 9%. Common: New common equity will be raised only by retaining earnings. Required: - I. Find the component costs of debt, preferred stock, and common stock. - II. What is the WACC? [09] (a) Discuss the operating cycle and the cash conversion cycle. How do these cycles affect a company's liquidity and working capital requirements? [03] (b) Compare and contrast aggressive, conservative, and moderate working capital policies. What are the risks and benefits associated with each policy? [04] (c) The board of directors of Aravind mills limited request you to prepare a statement showing the working capital requirements for a level of activity of 30,000 units of output for the year. The cost structure for the company's product for the above-mentioned activity level is given below. Data:Additional Information: - I. Past experience indicates that raw materials are held in stock, on an average for 2 months. - II. Work in progress (100% complete in regard to materials and 50% for labour and overheads) will be half a month's production. - III. Finished goods are in stock on an average for 1 month. - IV. Credit allowed to suppliers: 1 month. - V. Credit allowed to debtors: 2 months. - VI. A minimum cash balance of Rs 25,000 is expected to be maintained.Required: Prepare a statement of working capital requirements. [08] (a) Explain the concept of mutually exclusive projects. How should a firm decide between two mutually exclusive projects? [03] (b) Why is NPV considered a superior method for evaluating capital investment projects? [03] (c) Mr. Solaiman is responsible for considering two investment projects for his firm, each of which requires an up-front expenditure of Tk 25 million. You estimate that the cost of capital is 10% and that the investments will produce the following after-tax cash flows (in millions of taka): Data:Required: - I. What is the regular payback period for each of the projects? - II. What is the discounted payback period for each of the projects? - III. If the two projects are independent and the cost of capital is 10%, which project or projects should the firm undertake? - IV. If the two projects are mutually exclusive and the cost of capital is 5%, which project should the firm undertake? - V. If the two projects are mutually exclusive and the cost of capital is 15%, which project should the firm undertake? - VI. What is the crossover rate? [09] (a) Define optimal capital structure. Briefly outline the four primary factors that influence the capital structure decisions. [05] (b) Briefly explain the (i) MM theory; (ii) Trade-off theory; and (iii) the Signaling theory. [05] (c) The Weaver Watch Company sells watches for $25, the fixed costs are $140,000, and variable costs are $15 per watch. i) What is the breakeven point? Illustrate by means of a chart. ii) What would happen to the breakeven point if the selling price was raised to $31? What is the significance of this analysis? [05] Write Notes on: (i) Business risk and its determinants (ii) Operating leverage (iii) Stand-alone and portfolio risk and their measures (iv) Factors influencing dividend policy (v) Weighted average cost of capital. [15] Tracking Ref: ACC 302 / FCC 209 | BBA 5th Semester 2021 (a) Define financial management. Why is it necessary for business students who do not plan to major in finance to understand the basics of finance? [05] (b) "The ultimate goal of a business firm is to maximize wealth, not to maximize profit." Explain the statement logically. [05] (c) What do you mean by agency problem? What are some mechanisms that encourage managers to act in the best interests of stockholders? [05] (a) Define risk. Distinguish between business risk and financial risk. [04] (b) In general, can the riskiness of a portfolio be reduced to zero by increasing the number of stocks in the portfolio? Explain. [03] (c) Intex corporation is considering three possible capital projects for the next year. Each project has a 1year life and project returns depend on next year's state of the economy. The estimated rates of return are shown in the table: Also assume that Intex Corporation is going to invest one-third of its available funds in each project. Intex corporation will create a portfolio of three equally weighted projects. - i. Find each project's expected rate of return, variance and standard deviation. - ii. What is the expected rate of return, variance and standard deviation of the three project's portfolio? [08] (a) Which method of calculating the cost of equity shares would be most appropriate for the following firms: [04] i. A profitable firm that has never paid a dividend, but has had steady growth in earnings. ii. An electricity company that has paid a dividend every year for the last eighty years. (b) Two firm, F-1 and F-2. The firm F-1 has no debt and is totally financed by equity capital. The firm F-2 has Tk 2,000,000 outstanding debt and pays an interest rate of 10%. The firm's net income after-taxes are calculated using three tax rates, 0, 25 and 50 percent and the resulting values of net incomes are compared. Assume that the earnings before interest and taxes of both firms is Tk 1,000,000 each. Calculate cost of debt. [07] (c) Robi is currently selling for Tk 60 a share. The firm is expected to earn Tk 5.40 per share this year and to pay a year-end dividend of Tk 3.60. i. If investors require a 9 percent return, what rate of growth must be expected for Robi? ii. If Robi reinvests retained earnings in projects whose average return is equal to the stock's expected rate of return, what will be next year's EPS? [Hint: g = (1-Payout rate)(ROE).] [04] (a) Define working capital and working capital management. Discuss the significance of working capital management policy in case of a manufacturing enterprise. [06] (b) From the following information extracted from the books of Zahin Textile Ltd compute the operating cycle in days and the amount of working capital required: (a) What is profitability index? Which one is the superior ranking criterion, profitability index (PI) or net present value (NPV)? Explain. [04] (b) Edelman Engineering is considering including two pieces of equipment, a truck and an overhead pulley system, in this year's capital budget. The projects are independent. The cash outlay for the truck is $17,100, and that for the pulley system is $22,430. The firm's cost of capital is 14%. After-tax cash flows, including depreciation, are as follows: Calculate the IRR, the NPV, and the MIRR for each project, and indicate the correct accept/reject decision for each. [07] (c) Explain why, if two mutually exclusive projects are being compared, the short term project might have the higher ranking under the NPV criterion if the cost of capital is high, but the long-term project might be deemed better if the cost of capital is low. Would changes in the cost of capital ever cause a change in the IRR ranking of two such projects? [04] (a) Explain the logic of the residual dividend model, the steps a firm would take to implement it, and why it is more likely to be used to establish a long-run payout target than to set the actual year-by-year payout ratio. [05] (b) The Well Corporation expects next year's net income to be Tk 150 million. The firm's debt ratio is currently 40 percent. Well has Tk 120 million of profitable investment opportunities, and it wishes to maintain its existing debt ratio. According to the residual dividend model, how large should Well's dividend payout ratio be next year? Assume the firm uses only debt and common equity in its capital structure. [05] (c) After a 5-for-1 stock split, the Startech Company paid a dividend of TK 0.75 per new share, which represents a 9 percent increase over last year's pre-split dividend. What was last year's dividend per share? [05] (a) Write short notes on: i. Optimal Capital Structure ii. EBIT-EPS analysis [05] (b) State the main duties and powers of the CFOs of public sector enterprises in Bangladesh. How economic efficiency of Bangladesh can be enhanced by the use of modern capital budgeting techniques? [05] (c) Discuss the problems of financing in private sector enterprises of Bangladesh. Suggest some remedies to overcome those problems. [05]

item.title: PYQ ACC 303
item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester Standard Format: 4 Hours | 75 Marks | Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially.Tracking Ref: ACC 303 | BBA 5th Semester 2025 (a) State the steps involved in a sample survey. [04] (b) What is Sampling? Explain different types of sampling techniques. [03] (c) Under which circumstances, stratified random sampling design is considered to be appropriate? How would you select such a sample? [04] (d) Explain the meaning and significance of the concept of "Standard Error" in sampling. [04] (a) Differentiate between point estimation and interval estimation. Explain the characteristics of a good Estimator. [04] (b) What are the important points that should be considered before estimating the sample size? [03] (c) If we want to draw a simple random sample from a population of 4000 items, how large a sample you need to draw if you desire to estimate the percent defective within 2% of the true value with 95% probability. [04] (d) The foreman of a certain mining company has estimated the average quantity of ore extracted to be 34.6 tons per shift and the sample standard deviation to be 2.8 tons per shift, based upon a random selection of 6 shifts. Construct 95% confidence interval for the average quantity of ore extracted per shift. [04] (a) Define an estimator and an estimate. [02] (b) Mention the methods of finding the estimators and explain those briefly with example. [08] (c) The length (in millimeters) of cuckoo eggs found in hedge sparrow nests can be modeled with a common distribution. Consider the following data set: 22.0, 23.9, 20.9, 23.8, 25.0, 24.0, 21.7, 23.8, 22.8, 23.1, 23.1, 23.5, 23.0, 23.0 Required: Find the MLEs (Maximum Likelihood Estimators) of and . [05] (a) Write down the name of some parametric and non-parametric tests. [03] (b) What are the assumptions of Chi-square test? [03] (c) A public opinion poll surveyed a simple random sample of voters to establish whether there is a relationship between gender and voting preference. Respondents were classified by gender (male and female) and by voting preference (Republican, Democrat or Independent). Results are shown below. Required: - i. What is the best statistical test for analyzing the data? - ii. State the null hypothesis of the study. - iii. At 5% significance level, does the data support the null hypothesis? - iv. Interpret your results. [09] (a) What is a stochastic disturbance term? Write down the significance of a stochastic disturbance term in regression analysis. [05] (b) What is ordinary least squares (OLS) method? How will you estimate the regression coefficients using ordinary least squares method in a simple regression analysis? [05] (c) Explain the properties of ordinary least squares (OLS) method. [05] (a) What do you mean by the multi-collinearity problem in a multiple regression model? Explain different sources of multi-collinearity problem. [05] (b) What are the practical consequences of multi-collinearity problem in regression analysis? [05] (c) How multi-collinearity problem in a multiple regression model can be detected? Explain its remedial measures. [05] A computer output of the statistical analysis is given below:Descriptive StatisticsCorrelationsModel Summarya. Predictors: (Constant), Fixed Capital, EmploymentANOVAa. Dependent Variable: GDP b. Predictors: (Constant), Fixed Capital, EmploymentCoefficientsa. Dependent Variable: GDPRequired: (a) Calculate partial correlation coefficients. (b) Determine 95% confidence interval for partial regression coefficients. (c) Interpret above results. [15] Tracking Ref: ACC 303 | BBA 5th Semester 2024 (a) What is sampling? Explain the importance of sampling in solving business problem. [05] (b) Explain different types of sampling along with their situational suitability. [05] (c) What is sampling error? Describe different types of sampling errors. [05] (a) What is estimation? Distinguish between point and interval estimation. [03] (b) Suppose the following ten values represent random observations from a normal parent population of size 500: 2, 6, 7, 9, 5, 1, 0, 3, 5, 4. i. Make an estimate of the standard deviation of the population from the sample standard deviation. ii. Work out the standard error of mean for this finite population. iii. If the desired confidence level is 95, what will be the upper and lower limits of the confidence interval for the mean number of accidents per intersection per year? [07] (c) Given is the following information: Universe with N = 10,000. Variance of weight of the cereal containers on the basis of past records = 8 kg. i. Determine the size of the sample for estimating the true weight of the containers if the estimate should be within 0.4 kg. of the true average weight with 95% probability. ii. What would be the size of the sample if infinite universe is assumed? [05] (a) The procedure of testing hypothesis requires a researcher to adopt several steps. Describe in brief all such steps. [03] (b) A manufacturer considers his production process to be working properly if the mean length of the rods the manufactures is 8.5". The standard deviation of the rods always runs about 0.26". Suppose a sample of 64 rods is taken and this gives a mean length of rods equal to 8.6". What are the null and alternative hypotheses for this problem? Can you infer at 5% level of significance that the process is working properly? [04] (c) A drug research experimental unit is testing two drugs newly developed to reduce blood pressure levels. The drugs are administered to two different sets of animals. In group one, 350 of 600 animals tested respond to drug one and in group two, 260 of 500 animals tested respond to drug two. The research unit wants to test whether there is a difference between the efficacy of the said two drugs at 5 per cent level of significance. How will you deal with this problem? [04] (d) A sample of 10 is drawn randomly from a certain population. The sum of the squared deviations from the mean of the given sample is 50. Test the hypothesis that the variance of the population is 5 at 5 per cent level of significance. [04] (a) Write down the procedure of testing hypothesis. [03] (b) Define Chi-Square test. Write down the conditions for the application of Chi-square test. [05] (c) A sample of 200 people with a particular disease was selected. Out of these 100 were given a drug and the others were not given any drug. The results are as follows: Test whether the drug is effective or not. (The table value of for 1 d.f. at 5% level of significance is 3.84) [07] (a) What is the stochastic disturbance term? Discuss its significance in the regression analysis. [05] (b) What is ordinary least square method? Discuss the properties of OLS estimators. [05] (c) Mention the assumptions underlying the method of least squares in the classical linear regression model. [05] (a) You are given the following information: , , and , , and , , , On the basis of above information i. construct 95% confidence interval for and . ii. Write down the linear regression model. [04] (b) What is multicollinearity? Discuss the practical consequences of multicollinearity. [06] (c) How multicollinearity can be detected? [05] A computer output of the statistical analysis are given below:Descriptive StatisticsCorrelationsModel SummaryANOVAa. Predictors: (Constant), X1, X2 b. Dependent Variable: YCoefficientsWhere, Y = Total Personal Consumption Expenditure X1 = Expenditure on durable goods X2 = Expenditure on nondurable goodsRequirements: (a) Interpret the results. (b) Calculate all partial correlation coefficients. [15] Tracking Ref: ACC 303 | BBA 5th Semester 2023 (a) What is sampling? Discuss different types of sampling. [02] (b) Write down principal steps in sample survey. [04] (c) Distinguish between Sampling and Non-sampling Errors. [04] (d) What are the basic methods of drawing a Simple Random Sample? Describe one of them. [05] (a) Define the following terms: Null Hypothesis and Alternative hypothesis, Type I Error and Type II Error, One Tailed and Two Tailed test. [03] (b) A claim is made that a batch of bulbs has a mean life of 2800 hrs. From the past experience it is known that the SD of the life time is 100 hrs. A buyer specifies that he wants to test the claim against the alternative that the mean burning time is in fact below 2800 hrs. at 5% level of significance. A sample of size 25 is drawn and sample average is found to be 2750 hrs. Should the buyer accept the hypothesis that the mean life time of all bulbs in the population is 2800 hrs.? [04] (c) A company interested to knowing if there is a difference in the average salary received by foreman in two divisions. Accordingly, sample of 12 foreman in the first division and 10 from the second division are selected at random. Based upon the experience of the foreman's salaries are known to be approximately normally distributed, and the standard deviations are about the same. [05] (d) The coefficient of correlation obtained from a random sample of 18 pairs of values is 0.45. Is this significant of correlation in the population? [03] (a) Define estimation and distinguish between different types of estimation. [03] (b) From a random sample of 50 civil service personnel, the mean age and the sample standard deviation were found to be 40 years and 4.5 years respectively. Construct a 95 percent confidence interval for the mean age of civil servants. [04] (c) Discuss technique of testing hypothesis using confidence interval approach. [04] (d) Determine the size of the sample for estimating the true weight of the cereal containers for the universe with N = 5000 on the basis of the following information: i. the variance of weight = 4 ounces on the basis of past records. ii. estimate should be within 0.8 ounces of the true average weight with 99% probability. Will there be a change in the size of the sample if we assume infinite population in the given case? If so, explain by how much? [04] (a) What is Analysis of Variance? Mention assumptions involved in it. [03] (b) The following table gives the retail prices of a commodity in some shops selected in three big cities: Carry out the analysis of variance to find out whether there is a significant difference in the price charged in these cities. [06] (c) Two research workers classified some people in income groups on the basis of sampling studies. Their results are as follows: Show that the sampling technique of at least one research worker is defective. [06]You are given the Weekly Consumption Expenditure (Y) and the Income (X) of a sample of 10 families:Requirements: (Consider Y as the dependent variable) (a) Estimate the parameters of this model. (b) Determine the standard errors of the estimates. (c) Construct 95% confidence intervals for coefficients. (d) Test hypothesis for linear regression coefficient equal to 0.50. [15] (a) What is Multicollinearity? What are its practical consequences? [05] (b) How does one detect multicollinearity? [05] (c) What remedial measures can be taken to alleviate the problem of multicollinearity? [05] Consider the following tables showing the computer output of three variables analysis:Model Summarya. Predictors: (Constant), TFR, PGNP, FLFPANOVAa. Dependent Variable: CM b. Predictors: (Constant), TFR, PGNP, FLFPCoefficientsa. Dependent Variable: CMCorrelationsWhere CM = Child mortality, PGNP = Per capita GNP, FLFP = Female Labor Force Participation, and TFR = Total Fertility Rate.Required: (a) Calculate partial correlation coefficients , , and . [Consider PGNP = 2, FLFP = 3, and TFR = 4] (b) Interpret Outputs. [15] Tracking Ref: FCC 201 | BBA 3rd Semester 2021 (Applied Business Statistics) (a) Give classical definition of probability. Write down the laws of probability. [04] (b) A study showed that 75% of managers had some business education and 55% had engineering education. Further, 35% of the managers had some business education but no engineering education. i. What is the probability that a manager has some business and engineering education? ii. It is known that a manager has some engineering education, what is the probability that he has some business education? [04] (c) Eastern Apartments has a large number of units available to rent each month. A concern of management is the number of vacant apartments each month. A recent study revealed the percent of the time that a given number of apartments are vacant. Compute the average and standard deviation of number of vacant apartments. - i. Compute the mean number of vacant apartments each month. - ii. Compute the variance of the number of vacant apartments each month. **[07]** (a) What is sampling? Distinguish between probability sampling and non-probability sampling. [03] (b) Define Estimation. Distinguish among different types of estimates. [04] (c) A random sample of 200 measurements from an infinite population gave a mean value of 50 and a standard deviation of 9. Determine the 99% confidence limits for the mean value of the population. [04] (d) What should be the size of the sample if a simple random sample from a population of 4000 items is to be drawn to estimate the percent defective within 2 percent of the true value with 95.5 per cent probability? [04] (a) Eight coins were tossed 256 times and the following results were obtained: Are the coins biased? Use test. [07] (b) A company selects 9 salesmen at random and their sales figures for the previous month are recorded. They then undergo a course devised by a business consultant and their sales figure for the following month are compared as shown in the following table. Has the training course caused an improvement in the salesmen's ability? Use 5% level of significance. [08] (a) Write down the assumptions taken for the validity of the F-test in ANOVA. [02] (b) Set up an analysis of variance table for the following two-way design results: Per Acre Production Data of Wheat (in metric tons) Also state whether variety differences are significant at 5% level. [10] (c) A machine puts out 16 imperfect articles in a sample of 500. After machine is overhauled, it puts out 3 imperfect articles in a batch of 100. Has the machine improved? Test at 5% level of significance. [03] (a) What is statistical quality control? Write down its uses. [03] (b) Distinguish between product control and process control. [02] (c) Track Bicycle Parts manufacturer precision ball bearings for wheel hubs, bottom brackets, head sets, and pedals. Seth Adams is responsible for quality control at Track. He has been checking the output of the 5-mm bearings used in front wheel hubs. For each of the last 10 hours, he has sampled 5 bearings, with the following results: - i. Construct control charts for mean and the range to help Seth determine whether the production of 5-mm bearings is in control. - ii. Should Seth conclude that the process is in control? **[10]** (a) In a certain town, male and female each from 50% of the population. It is known that 30% of the males and 7% of the females are unemployed. A research student studying the employment situation selects an unemployed person at random. What is the probability that the person so selected is (a) male (b) female? [04] (b) Define normal distribution. What are its characteristics? Show the area under the normal curve. [06] (c) A factory produces a mechanism which consists of three independently manufactured parts. It is known that 1% of part 1, 4% of part 2 and 3% of part 3 are defective. What is the probability that a complete mechanism is not defective? [05] (a) Briefly state the steps of hypothesis testing? [05] (b) What is the difference between type-1 error and type-2 error? [03] (c) The mean production of wheat of a sample of 100 fields in 200 lbs. per acre with a standard deviation of 10 lbs. Another samples of 150 fields gives the mean of 220 lbs. with a standard deviation 12 lbs. Can the two samples be considered to have been taken from the same population whose standard deviation is 11 lbs.? Use 5% level of significance. [05] (d) Define test of proportion? [02]

item.title: PYQ ACC 305
item.description: Institution: University of Chittagong | Department: Department of Accounting Program: BBA 5th Semester Standard Format: 4 Hours | 75 Marks | Answer any FIVE questions sequentially/serially.Tracking Ref: Course Code ACC-305 | BBA 5th Semester (a) Define ‘Assurance Engagement’ and explain the key elements of an assurance engagement. [04] (b) Differentiate between reasonable and limited assurance, can an audit of financial statements provide absolute assurance? Justify your answer with appropriate reasons. [04] (c) Describe the meaning of the “expectations gap” in the context of auditing. Suggest appropriate steps that may help in minimizing the expectations gap between auditors and users of financial statements. [04] (d) What is “Lowballing”? Point out the factors that an auditor should consider before accepting an audit engagement. [03] In professional audit practice, it is important to agree on the terms of engagement before any assignments are taken up. This ensures a clear understanding between the auditor and the client. In such a context, you are required to: (a) Examine the key components of an audit engagement letter. [06] (b) Evaluate the factors to be considered during the assignment of the audit engagement team. [04] (c) Distinction among appointment letter, proposal letter, and engagement letter. Discuss the conditions and stages at which they are prepared and state the objectives of each. [05] (a) Briefly discuss the duties of auditors according to Section 213 of the Companies Act, 1994. [05] (b) An auditor discovers a material misstatement in a client’s financial statements but is under pressure from the client to overlook it, as it could jeopardize a significant contract. In this scenario, how should the auditor respond to this situation, considering the ethical standards for professional accountants? [05] (c) State the objectives, powers, and functions of the Financial Reporting Council under sections 7 and 8 of the Financial Reporting Act, 2015. [05] (a) What is audit risk? What are the different types of audit risk? [03] (b) Briefly explain the components of the internal control system as set out in ISA 315, ‘Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement’. [05] (c) Define the term ‘Assertion’ from the perspective of a financial audit. Describe the assertions related to ‘revenue’ and ‘receivables’ for conducting a financial audit. [07] (a) In accordance with ISA 500-Audit Evidence, explain the meaning of ‘sufficiency’ and ‘appropriateness’ of audit evidence, and discuss the various audit procedures for obtaining such evidence. [05] (b) Your firm XYZ & Co. Chartered Accountants, has been appointed as the auditor of Merry Company Limited (MCL) for the financial year ended 31 March 2025. You have been assigned as the engagement manager. During discussions with management, you were informed that MCL has recently received a significant number of requests for credit notes due to customers alleging that goods were received in poor condition. Therefore, Management of MCL intends to strengthen controls over the dispatch of goods and confirmation of their condition upon delivery. Again, you were informed that the directors of MCL have recently discovered that the store manager has been committing fraud. As part of her responsibilities, she was in charge of ordering inventory. She created fictitious purchase orders to non-existent suppliers, recorded false goods received notes for deliveries that never occurred, and submitted fake supplier invoices to the accounts department for payment.
